_comment: Translator context for en.json / en.manual.json keys: key -> one sentence saying which surface the string appears on and which sense of the English is meant. A SIDECAR, never inline. VS Code's translation key is `message + "/" + comment`, so adding or editing an inline comment there orphans every existing translation of that string; a separate file makes a description free to write and improve at any time. GNOME/KDE reach the same conclusion from the freeze side: "addition of a comment aimed for translators" is exempt from a string freeze, but "adding a context marker (msgctxt) is also subject to the freeze as it renders the affected string 'fuzzy'". Add an entry whenever a key's English is shorter than its meaning - an abbreviation, a bare unit, a key cap, or a word that is both a noun and a verb. Do NOT add one for a sentence fragment (`of`, `at`, `by`, `via`): a fragment needs deleting in Phase 3, and describing it only legitimises it. Coverage of the opaque class is gated at zero by contextSidecar.test.ts: every abbreviation, unit and key cap must carry an entry.

entries.components.appstore.categoryRail.all_ins: Row under the Discover rail's install-state heading that clears that filter, so the app list shows apps whether or not they are installed; not a select-all action.
entries.apps.builtinAppRoute.refused_page_title: Heading on a builtin page whose registration the build refused; {{route}} is the URL path the reader asked for, such as /aim, and is never translated.
entries.apps.builtinAppRoute.refused_page_lead: Plain-language explanation on that refused page: the product turned this page down while starting up because the assembled copy sets the page up wrongly, and nothing the reader does on the page can undo it. "Rejected" is the product refusing to register the page, not a permission denial and not a setting anyone could switch back on; "set up wrongly in this copy" means the defect is in the build that was assembled, not in the reader's configuration.
entries.apps.builtinAppRoute.refused_page_detail: Label above the raw registration diagnostic on that refused page, marking the text beneath it as addressed to the person who assembled this copy of the product rather than to the reader.
entries.apps.builtinAppRoute.refused_page_handof: Sentence directly above the page's only button, stating what that button does: it opens a chat with the agent and the diagnostic shown above is carried into it. Visible text rather than a tooltip, because it is the only action on the page.
entries.memoryV2.edit_action: Verb on the private member memory action that opens an editor; it does not save or approve a fact immediately.
entries.memoryV2.replaced_at: Date column showing when an experience was replaced by a fact and removed from current recall.
entries.memoryV2.replaced_by: Column naming the fact that replaced a saved experience; the experience remains recoverable.
entries.memoryV2.times_replaced: Count of replacement events for one recoverable experience, including replacement again after restoration.
entries.memoryV2.filter_all: Memory browser filter that includes facts, rules and experiences from the currently selected store.
entries.memoryV2.source_user: Memory record source badge identifying the human user who explicitly supplied or corrected this knowledge.
entries.memoryEditing.restore_now: Column heading in the restore-to-earlier-version preview of a memory record, over the value the record holds at this moment; paired with the "After restoring" column. An adverb of time meaning "currently", not a "do it now" button.

entries.app.dsk: Abbreviation for "disk" in the dashboard header's resource strip, followed by a percentage. Width-constrained: keep it as short as the target language allows.
entries.app.mem: Abbreviation for "memory" (RAM) in the dashboard header's resource strip, followed by a percentage. Width-constrained: keep it as short as the target language allows.
entries.app.metrics_card_cores_one: Logical CPU core count of the machine whose readings the header's system-metrics card shows, after its OS name ("macOS · 1 core"). "Core" is a processor core, not "central" or "essential". Singular form.
entries.app.metrics_card_cores_other: Logical CPU core count of the machine whose readings the header's system-metrics card shows, after its OS name ("macOS · 10 cores"). "Core" is a processor core, not "central" or "essential". Plural form.
entries.app.nav_back: Top-bar route-history Back arrow's accessible name and tooltip, and the shortcuts-modal row for Cmd/Ctrl+Left. Browser-back sense (navigation history), not 'return an item'.
entries.app.nav_back_title: Tooltip for the top-bar Back arrow while keyboard shortcuts are enabled, on Windows/Linux. Label plus the chord after a middot, like app.focus_mode_title; translate the label and the modifier name (de: Strg), keep the arrow glyph.
entries.app.nav_back_title_mac: macOS variant of app.nav_back_title — the chord uses the ⌘ glyph; translate only the label.
entries.app.nav_forward: Top-bar route-history Forward arrow's accessible name and tooltip, and the shortcuts-modal row for Cmd/Ctrl+Right. Browser-forward sense (navigation history).
entries.app.nav_forward_title: Tooltip for the top-bar Forward arrow while keyboard shortcuts are enabled, on Windows/Linux. Same shape as app.nav_back_title.
entries.app.nav_forward_title_mac: macOS variant of app.nav_forward_title — the chord uses the ⌘ glyph; translate only the label.
entries.app.nav_back_history: Accessible name of the menu that opens on right-click or long-press of the top-bar Back arrow: the list of earlier pages and sessions the user can jump to. Browser-history sense.
entries.app.nav_forward_history: Accessible name of the menu that opens on right-click or long-press of the top-bar Forward arrow: the list of later pages and sessions. Same shape as app.nav_back_history.
entries.app.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.apps.autoImprovement.findingDetail.red: The gate stage named "RED": the reproducing test FAILS on unmodified code, which is what proves the defect is real. A protocol token the app also prints in logs and commit notes, so keep the Latin form; it is not the colour.
entries.apps.autoResearch.researchLabPage.30s: A preset duration of 30 seconds. The number is data; only the unit letter is translatable, and most locales keep `s`.
entries.apps.autoResearch.researchLabPage.60s: A preset duration of 60 seconds. The number is data; only the unit letter is translatable, and most locales keep `s`.
entries.apps.autoResearch.researchLabPage.add: Verb on the button that adds the typed sub-question to the research list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the sub-question. Distinct from the "Add" on the Code Review Sage page, which adds a review pattern.
entries.apps.autoResearch.researchLabPage.min: The unit "min" = minutes, rendered after a number. An abbreviation, not the word "minimum".
entries.apps.awsControl.console.access_forget: Button on a share-ledger row in the account console. The verb "forget": drop this link from the list. It does not revoke the link early — the honest wording is in the row's own copy.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.col_actions: Column header in the cloud drive's file table (AWS Control console), over the per-row action buttons (download, share, delete). The plural noun "actions"; matches the artifact library's Actions column.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.col_kind: Column header in the cloud drive's file table (AWS Control console), over the type badge (Folder, Widget, JSON…). The noun "kind" meaning type/category, not "kind" as in gentle; matches the artifact library's Kind column.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.col_modified: Column header in the cloud drive's file table (AWS Control console), over the last-changed timestamp. The past participle "modified" as a date heading; reuse the word this locale uses for the artifact library's Updated column.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.col_name: Column header in the cloud drive's file table (AWS Control console), over the file/folder name cells. The noun "name" as a table heading; matches the artifact library's Name column.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.col_size: Column header in the cloud drive's file table (AWS Control console), over the byte-size cells. The noun "size" (file size); short, it sits on a narrow column.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.expiry_1d: Option in the share dialog: the link expires one day after it is made. "1 day" as a duration; keep it short, it sits on a small button.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.expiry_1h: Option in the share dialog: the link expires one hour after it is made. "1 hour" as a duration; keep it short, it sits on a small button.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.expiry_7d: Option in the share dialog: the link expires seven days after it is made. "7 days" as a duration; keep it short, it sits on a small button.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.folder_create_fa: Error line shown when creating a folder in the cloud drive fails (AWS Control console). A short apology sentence; no folder was created.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.folder_delete_ac: Button label on the inline folder-delete confirm row (AWS Control console). The verb "delete" applied to a folder; parallel to "Delete file" (delete_confirm_action).
entries.apps.awsControl.console.folder_delete_co: Inline confirmation prompt before deleting a folder in the cloud drive (AWS Control console). {{name}} is the folder's name; the wording must make clear the folder AND everything inside it is removed. Mirrors the file delete_confirm on the same surface.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.folder_delete_fa: Error line shown when deleting a folder in the cloud drive fails (AWS Control console). A short apology sentence; the folder is unchanged.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.folder_name: Placeholder/label on the text input for naming a folder being created in the cloud drive (AWS Control console). The noun phrase "folder name", i.e. the name of a folder.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.folder_new: Button in the cloud drive toolbar (AWS Control console) that opens the new-folder name input. "New folder" as a create action; reuse this locale's artifact-library "New folder" wording.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.key_healthy: State text and dot label on a Connections row when the key passed its identity check. The adjective "healthy" describing the credential, paired with "Failed"; not a person's health.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.kind_folder: The Kind-cell value on a folder row in the cloud drive's file table (AWS Control console). The noun "folder" as a type label, paired with Widget/JSON/etc.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.kind_svg: Artifact-kind badge in the cloud drive's Library and its "Add from Artifacts" picker, naming a standalone vector image artifact. "SVG" is a file-format acronym: keep the form practitioners in the target language use (usually the Latin acronym, untranslated) and keep it short, since it sits in a compact badge beside labels like Widget and JSON.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.kind_text: Artifact-kind badge in the cloud drive's Library and its "Add from Artifacts" picker, naming a plain-text artifact. The noun "text" as a TYPE label (not the verb, and not "message"), paired with Widget/Markdown/JSON/SVG in the same row of badges; keep it short.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.kind_widget: Artifact-kind badge in the account console library. "Widget" is this product's word for a saved interactive HTML snippet; keep the term practitioners in the target language use for a UI widget.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.library_actions: Accessible name for the per-item overflow ("⋮") trigger on a card or row of the account console's Library folder, which lists what is stored in the cloud. The Library counterpart of file_actions and folder_actions -- match whatever construction you chose for those. Names the MENU, not any one action in it.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.library_add_onew: Shown at the top of the account console's "Add from Artifacts" dialog, warning that copying an item to the cloud uses storage the account pays for. It says only that: the same dialog carries a Remove control on its cards, so any claim that removal is unavailable would contradict a button under it. Must be SELF-CONTAINED — it may not refer to the "Where this lives" drawer, which is not visible while this dialog is open.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.library_all: Filter chip above the artifact library in the account console. Means "no kind filter — show every artifact", not "all" as a quantity or "select all".
entries.apps.awsControl.console.library_local_fa: Error shown in the account console when the list of the user's OWN artifacts (stored locally by Kiro) could not be read. Distinct from library_list_failed, which is the same failure for the copies stored in the cloud -- the folder joins the two, so both messages can appear and must not read alike. "artifacts" is the product's own term; use the word used for the Artifacts surface.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.library_open: Accessible name for a card in the account console's Library folder, which lists what is stored in the cloud. Activating the card opens that item on its own page in Artifacts -- the product surface listing things Kiro made for the user; translate "Artifacts" with the same word used for that surface's own title. {{name}} is the item's title.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.library_remove: Item in the overflow menu of a card or row in the account console's Library folder, which lists what is actually stored in the cloud. The verb "remove": delete this cloud copy (its objects and its local sync record). Offered on every listed copy, including one this machine never pushed, so do not word it as though it acted on a local item.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.library_remove_a: The danger button that carries out the removal, inside the confirm. "copy" is a NOUN -- the duplicate stored in the cloud -- not the verb "to copy". Sits beside sibling confirm buttons worded "Delete file" and "Delete folder", which restate their object the same way; keep it about that short.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.library_remove_c: Inline confirm prompt shown before the destructive library remove runs, naming the artifact via {{name}}. It asks the owner to approve deleting the cloud copy; keep the curly quotes around the name.

Second sentence of the library remove confirm, naming the bucket folder the delete will empty. {{folder}} is an S3 key prefix rendered as monospace code inside the <folder> tag -- keep the tag around the placeholder and do not translate or re-spell the path. Word order is free: place the folder wherever the sentence reads naturally, and end with your locale's full stop.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.library_removing: Replaces the removal button's label while the request is in flight, so it must read as an action IN PROGRESS rather than as a noun for the act of removing. Pairs with the sibling library_adding; use the same construction your language chose there.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.library_stale_li: Warning on a LIST ROW in the account console's Library folder: the copy stored in the cloud is an older version than the one on this computer. The sibling key library_stale_preview says the same thing for a GRID CARD and mentions the card's preview picture; a row has no preview, so this variant must not mention one. {{version}} is the cloud copy's version number, rendered after a literal v.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.share: Button beside a file in the account console's drive. The verb "share": open a dialog that mints a time-boxed download link. Not the noun "a share".
entries.apps.awsControl.console.stat_this_month: Label on a stat card in the account console showing this calendar month's AWS spend so far. "This month" as a time window, paired with a currency figure beneath it.
entries.apps.awsControl.page.aggregate_healthy_o: Third part of the one-line aggregate under the Accounts page title ("N accounts · M keys · H healthy"). Counts credential profiles that passed their identity check; the adjective "healthy" as a count label.

Third part of the one-line aggregate under the Accounts page title ("N accounts · M keys · H healthy"). Counts credential profiles that passed their identity check; the adjective "healthy" as a count label (plural form).
entries.apps.awsControl.page.keys_summary_one: Right-aligned summary on an account row in the dense Accounts list, counting the account's credential profiles. "Keys" is this app's plain word for credential profiles; the singular form for exactly one.
entries.apps.awsControl.page.keys_summary_other: Right-aligned summary on an account row in the dense Accounts list, counting the account's credential profiles. "Keys" is this app's plain word for credential profiles; the plural form.
entries.apps.awsControl.page.kind_sso: Badge on a credential profile chip in AWS Control, naming the profile's credential type. "SSO" = AWS IAM Identity Center single sign-on; keep the acronym practitioners in the target language use and keep it short, since it sits in a compact chip beside the region.
entries.apps.codeReviewSage.components.addReposM: Button on the add-repositories dialog. A VERB: adds the typed repository to the app's pinned set. Not the noun 'an add'.
entries.apps.codeReviewSage.components.bandChips: Filter chip above the report's findings list. Means 'no band filter — show every severity', not 'all' as a quantity.
Version chip in the app rail's identity row, e.g. "v2.0". `{{version}}` is the number — keep the prefix short, and drop it entirely if your locale does not prefix version numbers.
entries.apps.codeReviewSage.components.prPickLis: Badge on a pull request in the picker, marking one that appeared since the last review of this repository. An ADJECTIVE describing the pull request.
entries.apps.codeReviewSage.components.reviewCha: Speaker label above the reader's own question in the Code Review Sage chat transcript, paired with "Reviewer" for the agent's replies; the second-person pronoun addressing the current user, not the possessive "your".
entries.apps.commandBar.action_ask: Footer of the Command Bar launcher, naming what pressing Enter will do to the highlighted row: hand the text the user typed to the agent — into the open conversation's composer, or a new conversation when none is open. A VERB in the imperative ('ask this'), not the noun 'an ask' and not 'a question'. It alternates with Run, Open, Open View and Open Session as the selection moves, so keep the same grammatical form and a similar length as those.
entries.apps.commandBar.action_run: Footer of the Command Bar launcher, naming what pressing Enter will do to the highlighted row: run that command in place. A VERB in the imperative ('run this'), not the noun 'a run' and not 'execute a program'. It sits beside a return-key cap on a single muted line and alternates with Open, Open View and Open Session as the selection moves, so keep all four the same grammatical form and a similar length.
entries.apps.commandBar.kind.app: Right-aligned kind label on a Command Bar row, in a column with "Command", "Setting" and "View". Short for a Kiro Crew APP -- an installed extension such as Dev Fleet or Meetings -- so the row opens that app, not a generic program and not a mobile app. A noun naming what the row is. Keep it short: the label shares the row with the title and subtitle and is the first thing truncated.
entries.apps.crewCompanion.breathe.end: Label on the button that stops the breathing exercise before it finishes, inside the exercise overlay. An imperative verb ("stop this now"), not the noun "the end" — several languages use different words for the two.
entries.apps.crewCompanion.header.desktop_tip: Hint under the Crew Companion page subtitle when the desktop overlay is running. Tells the user they can click the sprite to open its panel and right-click to change its avatar. It must NOT tell them to quit from that menu: turning the companion off is now a button on this page.
entries.apps.crewCompanion.menu.quit: Label shared by the pet's right-click menu item and the Turn off button on the Crew Companion dashboard page. Both POST the app-disable endpoint. An imperative verb ("stop it now"), not the adjective "disabled".
entries.apps.crewCompanion.offline.couldnt_turn_: Failure notice after the Crew Companion page's Turn off button cannot reach POST /api/apps/crew-companion/disable. {{error}} is the server's reason. Same shape as couldnt_open.
entries.apps.crewCompanion.reminders.add_button: Button that saves the reminder typed in the box beside it. The verb "add", not the arithmetic sense.
entries.apps.crewCompanion.settings.custom_place: Placeholder in a small number field for a custom break interval. Short for "minutes" (the unit), not "minimum".
entries.apps.crewCompanion.time.now: Relative time label on a reminder that is due at this moment, shown where others read "20 min from now".
entries.apps.crewCompanion.view.everyMinShort: Placeholder inside the small number field for a CUSTOM break interval, in the companion panel's break-rhythm row beside the 30/45/60/90 preset buttons. Short for "minutes" (the unit), not "minimum". The field is only as wide as two or three digits, so keep it to the shortest form the target language has.
entries.apps.designCritique.askLayer.ask: Verb on the submit button of the "ask about this" popover in Design Critique: send the typed question about the highlighted finding. Not the noun ("an ask").
entries.apps.designCritique.composer.critique_th: Label of the button that starts a critique on the Design Critique composer, shown once two or more screenshots are staged. The count is how many are staged, and the critique covers the order they are in as well as each screen.
Label of the button that starts a critique on the Design Critique composer, shown when exactly one screenshot is staged.
entries.apps.designCritique.composer.unrecognise: Design Critique composer, said back to the user about what they just pasted: the input is not a Figma link, a code repository, an absolute local path or a serving URL. Describes the pasted reference, not the critique or the user, so an adjective agreeing with a masculine or feminine noun should agree with the local word for the pasted link or path.
entries.apps.designCritique.designCritiquePage.n: Verb-like button in the Design Critique rail header: start a new critique. The create sense, not a "recently added" badge.
entries.apps.designCritique.designCritiquePage.s: Last-resort error text used only when the thrown exception carries no message of its own. It is rendered alone on the composer's error line, so it has to read as a complete notice even though the English is lower-case.

Client-side timeout notice for the critique the user is watching: the run was not cancelled and continues on the server, so this must not be phrased as a failure. The shorter of two sibling timeout notices — this one drops the promise about resuming.

The same timeout situation as the sibling key ending in `_come`, reached from the background poll rather than the foreground run, which is why this variant also tells the user that coming back later resumes it.
entries.apps.designCritique.designCritiquePage.t: Fallback error for a failed review run with no message of its own. "Critique" is this app's noun for one review of one design, and is used as a countable noun throughout.
Rejection when more than twenty screenshots are sent in one go. "Screens" here means app screens or screenshots, never physical displays or monitors.
Fallback error for a failed discovery pass with no message of its own. "Scan" is that pass over a link, repo or URL looking for screens — nothing to do with security scanning.
Rejection shown when every file the user dropped or picked was filtered out for not having an image MIME type, so nothing was staged at all.
entries.apps.designCritique.scopingPicker.critiq: Label of the button that starts a critique on the scoping step, after the user has picked two or more of the discovered screens to audit as one flow. The count is how many are picked.
Label of the button that starts a critique on the scoping step, when exactly one of the discovered screens is picked.
entries.apps.designCritique.scopingPicker.pick_a: Disabled label of the scoping step's start button, shown while the user has picked nothing yet. It says what to do next, not what the button does.
entries.apps.designCritique.utils.i_ll_capture_i: The deployed-page counterpart of the dev-server tail, following the localised words for a live page and a middle dot. It omits the must-be-running warning because a deployed page is assumed up.
entries.apps.designCritique.utils.i_ll_clone_it_: Follows the localised word for a code repository and a middle dot in the Design Critique composer. "Screens" means app screens, never physical displays, and the second sentence is a limit rather than an error: a page needing a running server cannot be looked at.
entries.apps.designCritique.utils.i_ll_list_the_: Same limit as the repository variant but for a folder on this machine, and it drops the promise to clone because nothing is downloaded. Follows the localised words for local code and a middle dot.
entries.apps.designCritique.utils.i_ll_pull_the_: Design Critique composer, second half of the line said back about a pasted Figma link; the localised word for a Figma file and a middle dot come first, so this continues that line rather than opening one. "Frames" is Figma's own term for the artboards inside a file.
entries.apps.designCritique.utils.it_must_be_run: Follows the localised words for the user's own dev server and a middle dot, which is why the English begins lower-case and reads as a continuation. The subject of "it" is that server, and "capture" means take a screenshot of the page as it is served.
entries.apps.designCritique.utils.not_something_: The only one of these tails on the error path: it follows the localised word for Unrecognised and an em dash, and lists the four kinds of reference the field accepts. A pasted string matched none of them.
entries.apps.designTweak.devServer.use: Verb on the button that accepts the dev-server URL typed (or detected) beside it, so Design Tweak frames the preview from that server. Not the noun "use" and not "usage".
entries.apps.designTweak.projects.add: Verb on the button that registers the folder path typed beside it as a web app Design Tweak can preview. If the target language needs an object, name the app or folder.
entries.apps.designTweak.projects.dev_badge: Badge on a project row in Design Tweak's app dropdown, marking an app that is previewed from its running dev server. Short for "development server" and rendered lowercase; most locales keep the English `dev`, which is what the surrounding UI calls it.
entries.apps.issueRadar.components.labelPicker.a: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.apps.issueRadar.components.leftRail.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.apps.issueRadar.components.prBulkBar.mer: Confirmation line before an irreversible bulk merge, naming the exact pull requests and the merge strategy. `numbers` is a pre-formatted list of provider references (`#7, #8 and #9` on GitHub, `!7, !8 and !9` on GitLab) - do not translate or re-punctuate it. `method` is a Git merge STRATEGY name (`squash`) - keep it verbatim.
entries.apps.issueRadar.connectPanel.cli: "CLI" = command-line interface, naming a connection method the user picks. Keep the acronym practitioners in the target language use.
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.crews.editor.label: Chip at the end of the owned-labels row in the crew editor, which opens the label picker. A VERB in the sense of "attach another label to this crew's scope" — not the noun, and not arithmetic. It sits beside real label names, so it must read as an action rather than as one more label.
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.crews.editor.triag: First row of the Triage model dropdown in the crew editor, in the list of model names. Means "no triage model — this crew runs every turn on its work model": a setting that is switched off, not a power state and not "off" as in away.
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.crews.filter_all: First chip in the crew list's filter row, beside Working / Needs you / Paused. Means "no state filter — show every crew, including paused and retired ones", not "all" as a quantity or "whole".
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.crews.page.kind_ci: Badge on a line of a crew's work log, naming what that entry recorded: a continuous-integration run on the crew's pull request. "CI" = continuous integration — keep the acronym practitioners in the target language use, and keep it short: the badge sits in a fixed-width column beside longer labels like "Merged" and "Handed back".
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.crews.page.model_h: Button under the crew page notice that says a model picked in the crew's chat is kept. Means "let the crew go back to running its checks on the cheaper triage model, and switching to its work model when an issue needs work". Name that outcome. NOT the crew's Pause / Resume button beside it, which starts and stops the whole crew: keep the two clearly different.
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.graphView.led_read: Status LED label on a graph node: item is unblocked and ready to start. Abbreviation of "ready"; keep it 3-4 characters, silkscreen style.
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.graphView.led_run: Status LED label on a graph node: the crew is actively running on this item. Abbreviation of "running"; keep it 3-4 characters, silkscreen style.
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.settings.generalSe: Section HEADING (a noun: 'the refresh settings'), not the verb. The nearby repoSettings.refresh IS the verb on a button — five languages already translate the two differently, so do not reuse one word for both.
entries.apps.issueRadar.views.tagging.untaggedIs: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.apps.meetings.priority.low: Priority level of a meeting action item, the lowest of high/medium/low. An adjective describing importance, not volume or position.
entries.apps.meetings.settings.addTerm: Verb on a button: add a term to the meeting dictionary (the vocabulary list that improves transcription accuracy). If the target language needs an object, "add a term" is the sense.
entries.apps.meetings.settings.translationOff: The first option in the Meetings live-translation target-language PICKER, sitting above a list of language endonyms (English, 日本語, …) and meaning "do not translate". A choice in a dropdown, not a toggle's state label and not the preposition — several languages need a different word here than for an off switch.
entries.apps.meetings.taskSidebar.add: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.apps.mochi.approval.bubble_needs_approva: Speech bubble floating over the desktop pet when a tool is waiting on the user. {{pet}} is the pet's name, which the user can change in Settings, so it must stay a placeholder and must not be translated. {{purpose}} is a free-text sentence the AI agent wrote about what it is trying to do; it can be long, so keep the surrounding words short. The bubble is narrow.

Same desktop speech bubble as apps.mochi.approval.bubble_needs_approval, used when the agent stated no purpose. {{pet}} is the user-chosen pet name (do not translate). Keep it short: the bubble is narrow.
entries.apps.mochi.approval.risk_low: The LOW end of the risk scale (low / medium / high) on the pet's tool-approval dialog, rendered immediately before the word "risk". An adjective describing how dangerous the pending action is, not height or volume.
entries.apps.mochi.approval.trust_all_base: Button granting standing permission for a whole command family, e.g. every 'npm' command. {{base}} is one or more command names joined by ', ' (a piped command yields several). Middle of three trust options: wider than trust_this_command, narrower than trust_all_tools.
entries.apps.mochi.approval.trust_all_tools: Button granting standing permission for EVERY tool in this chat, not just the one being asked about. Widest of the three trust options, so the wording must feel broader than trust_this_command and trust_all_base. It must also name its SCOPE: the grant covers this chat session only. The same label doubles as the button on a card whose command could not be derived, where that one click IS the grant, so a reader who cannot see the scope consents to more than they meant to.
entries.apps.mochi.approval.trust_hint: One line under the approval buttons on a card whose command could not be derived, so the only trust available is the session-wide one. It describes what that Trust click does and deliberately names NO tool: the grant covers every later tool in the session, so naming the pending one would understate it.
entries.apps.mochi.approval.trust_this_command: Button granting standing permission for ONE exact command. The command itself is not in this string — it is passed as the child of the <mono/> component slot and rendered verbatim in a monospace code chip, already shortened with an ellipsis if long. Do not add {{cmd}} or any placeholder; the chip renders the command. Narrowest of three trust options; must read as narrower than apps.mochi.approval.trust_all_base and trust_all_tools.
entries.apps.mochi.settingsPanel.mcp_add: Button that adds a new MCP server row in the desktop pet's Settings window. The VERB "add", not the noun.
entries.apps.mochi.sprite.fps: Abbreviation for "frames per second", labelling a number input in the pet's spritesheet importer. Keep the conventional abbreviation for the target language rather than expanding it; the field is width-constrained.
entries.apps.mochi.watchPanel.priority.low: The LOW end of a watch item's priority scale (high / normal / low) in the pet's watch list. An adjective describing importance, not height or volume.
entries.apps.opsMissionControl.opsMissionControl: Autonomy-mode badge for the highest level, where the agent executes actions its rules grant. The imperative verb "act", one of three modes with "observe" and "propose"; not the noun ("an act").
entries.apps.opsMissionControl.settingsPanel.gh: The literal name of the GitHub CLI executable, `gh`, shown in monospace. Do not translate: the user types it.
entries.apps.opsMissionControl.settingsPanel.min: The unit "min" = minutes, rendered after a number in a staleness-timeout field. An abbreviation, not the word "minimum".
entries.apps.opsMissionControl.settingsPanel.mod: Label on the third segment of the autonomy-mode control in Ops Mission Control Settings, where the agent executes actions its rules grant. The imperative verb "act", alongside "Observe" and "Propose"; not the noun ("an act").
entries.apps.opsMissionControl.settingsPanel.off: State value meaning disabled, on a notification-channel or sync badge. Not the preposition or the adverb.
entries.apps.opsMissionControl.settingsPanel.who: The literal `who:` key of an on-call shift entry in the committed rotation.yaml file, shown in monospace. Do not translate: it names a YAML field the user edits.
entries.apps.papyrus.page.pdf: The file format "PDF", labelling the compiled output of a LaTeX paper. An acronym practitioners keep untranslated in nearly every locale.
entries.apps.papyrus.workspace.log: Noun: the LaTeX compiler's output log, naming a tab beside the PDF preview. A record of what the compiler printed — NOT the verb "to log" and not a logarithm.
entries.apps.personalShopper.preferencesTab.add: Submit button on the inline 'add a preference' form in the Personal Shopper Preferences tab. The VERB (commit this new preference), not the noun 'an addition'. The sibling add_group is the same verb applied to a group, so a language that inflects by object may need a different form.
entries.apps.pptxMaker.libraryPanel.font_specime: Type specimen shown large in the template preview, filled with that template's own theme font and text colour. Not a label: the two characters exist so the user can judge the TYPEFACE's letterforms at a glance, the role an "Aa" ramp plays in a font picker. Keep the Latin pair unless your readers would judge a typeface better from one upper- and one lower-case glyph of their own script; never render it as a word.
entries.apps.specBuilder.components.projectPicke: Spec Builder's project-folder picker: the button that navigates one directory level up. 'Up' means the parent folder, not upward motion or an increase.
entries.apps.specBuilder.components.specRail.act: Spec Builder's spec-list group header for specs that are still being planned (not yet at the tasks phase). Opposite of PLAN READY. Status of the work, not 'currently selected'.
entries.apps.specBuilder.components.specRail.v: Spec Builder's sidebar footer: the single-letter prefix before the app version number, as in v1.2.3. Short for version, not the letter itself.
entries.apps.specBuilder.components.specDetail.c: Dismiss the delete-spec confirmation without removing the spec. The verb on a dialog button, not the noun 'a cancellation'.
entries.apps.specBuilder.components.taskList.run: Verb on the button beside ONE task in Spec Builder's task list: have the agent do that single task and then stop. NOT the noun ("a run"), which several locales translate differently, and not "start the whole build" — the sibling "Start building" works the entire list.
entries.apps.workflows.workflowsPage.run: Verb on a button: execute this job/workflow now. NOT the noun ("a run"), which several locales translate differently.
entries.autoImprovement.prTitlePrefix: "PR" = pull request, prefixing a generated pull-request title. Keep the abbreviation the target language's developers actually use; do not expand it if that would break the layout.
entries.components.appstore.appListRow.github_st: aria-label on the star icon beside a third-party app's abbreviated GitHub stargazer count in the Discover list row. "Stars" as in GitHub repository stars (a popularity count), not a rating the user gives.
entries.components.appstore.featuredSpotlight.ge: Verb on an App Store button: install this app. Not the sense of obtain or receive.
entries.components.appstore.featuredSpotlight.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.edit_avatar: Button label and the accessible name of a clickable crew face: opens the avatar builder. "Edit" as an imperative verb; "avatar" is the crew's picture/face, same noun as field_label.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.hint_customize: One-time nudge chip shown beside a crew's face while it still wears the default, name-derived look. Same verb as edit_avatar on purpose (one action, one word); "this avatar" = the crew's face the chip sits next to, NOT the user's own picture. Friendly imperative, short enough for a pill.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.mode_picture: Tab label in the crew avatar builder: switches to the uploaded-picture tier. "Picture" as a noun (a photo/image the user uploads), not the verb.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.motion_nod: Name of one reaction motion in the crew avatar builder's Reactions tab, alongside Still, Bounce and Sparkle: the ghost tips forward and back once a turn finishes. The gesture of agreement/acknowledgement made by moving the head down and up — a noun here, and NOT the sense "doze off".
entries.components.avatarBuilder.opt_bow: Thumbnail label in the crew avatar builder's headwear tab: a decorative ribbon bow worn on the ghost's head. The noun "bow" as in hair ribbon — not the weapon, not the verb.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.opt_cap: Thumbnail label in the crew avatar builder's headwear tab: a baseball cap. The noun "cap" (hat), not a limit or the verb.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.opt_cat: Thumbnail label in the crew avatar builder's mouth tab: a cat-like ':3' mouth shape. The animal, describing the mouth's look.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.opt_mug: Thumbnail label in the crew avatar builder's prop tab: a steaming coffee mug the ghost holds. The drinking vessel, not the verb or the face.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.opt_oh: Thumbnail label in the crew avatar builder's mouth tab: a small round open mouth, as in saying "oh". An interjection; transliterate rather than translate if no equivalent.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.sound_pop: Name of one notification-sound preset in the crew avatar builder's Reactions tab, alongside Chime, Ding, Blip and Pulse. The short percussive sound a cork or a bubble makes; not the music genre and not the verb.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.tile_amber: Accessible color name for an avatar background swatch: the warm yellow-orange color, not the fossil resin.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.tile_coral: Accessible color name for an avatar background swatch: the pink-orange color, not the sea animal.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.tile_olive: Accessible color name for an avatar background swatch: the dull yellow-green color, not the fruit.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.tile_plum: Accessible color name for an avatar background swatch: the deep reddish-purple color, not the fruit.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.tile_red: Accessible color name for an avatar background swatch in the crew avatar builder: the color red.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.tile_rose: Accessible color name for an avatar background swatch: the pinkish color rose, not the flower.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.tile_steel: Accessible color name for an avatar background swatch: a muted gray-blue ("steel blue"), not the metal itself.
entries.components.crewLayout.element.git: Draggable palette tile and cell label in the composable-layout editor, naming the element that shows the Git view (branch, status, history) for the session's working directory. "Git" is the version-control product name — keep it verbatim, do not translate or transliterate.
entries.components.sidePanelLayout.more_below: Small label under a settings side list, shown while rows of the same list are hidden below the fold; it tells the reader to scroll. Not a button and not a more-options menu.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.agen: Usage evidence in a bounded monitor. A turn is one agent invocation caused by an actionable wake; {{count}} is already locale-formatted, so keep the label before it.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.desc: Explains the token-saving monitor: cheap provider probes run on a cadence, while the agent is invoked only when the probe finds actionable review work.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.gitl: Inline setup guidance after a valid self-managed GitLab merge-request URL is rejected because its host is absent from dashboard.gitlab_hosts. Tell the operator the host is not allowed and to add it in ~/.kiro/crew/config.json. Keep GitLab, dashboard.gitlab_hosts, and ~/.kiro/crew/config.json unchanged.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.inva: Inline validation for a non-empty URL that is not a supported GitHub.com, GitLab, Azure DevOps Services, or Bitbucket Cloud pull-request URL.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.late: Label for the provider probe's latest machine classification, such as pending or actionable; the value beside it is intentionally not translated.
Label for the monitor scheduler's latest machine decision, such as no_change or retry_provider; the value beside it is intentionally not translated.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.limi: Inline validation beside one bounded integer field. {{min}} and {{max}} are already locale-formatted numbers; preserve both placeholders.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.maxi: Budget field limiting how many agent invocations this monitor may cause before it stops; a turn is not a chat message.
Budget field limiting provider API failures before the monitor stops.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.moni: Accessible name for the monitor control. {{status}} is one of this namespace's translated statuses.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.obje: Label for the fixed outcome the monitor is trying to reach, not a general task description.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.prob: Usage evidence counting cheap provider checks, not agent invocations; {{count}} is already locale-formatted, so keep the label before it.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.prov: Inline validation when an edit changes the code host of an existing monitor. Explain without using the internal term provider: the monitor is tied to its current code host and the new link must be watched from a new session.
Usage evidence counting provider API failures; {{count}} is already locale-formatted, so keep the label before it.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.pull: Example pattern for a GitHub pull request URL field. Keep the GitHub URL unchanged and translate only the local equivalent of e.g.; keep the final ellipsis.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.revi: The fixed monitor objective: the pull request has no remaining actionable review work and is ready for human review or merge.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.sess: Shown on BOTH of the popover's views -- the bounded monitor form and the goal-loop form -- when the current chat is a crew or member session. It must therefore name automations in general rather than monitors, because on the goal form it explains dead goal fields. These modes route work through crew ingress and cannot safely host a direct agent turn.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.side: Compact chat-sidebar subtitle for a bounded monitor. {{status}} is translated separately; keep this short enough for a narrow row.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.stat: Live status: an actionable probe already woke the agent and that agent invocation is still running.
Live status: the monitor is armed and probing normally; it does not mean the agent is currently running.
Live status before the monitor's first provider probe has completed.
Live status while the scheduler waits through a provider retry delay after an error or busy response.
Terminal status: the monitor cannot safely continue or its stored record is invalid; it is not merely paused.
Terminal status: a configured runtime, turn, token, or provider-error limit stopped the monitor.
Terminal status: the pull request reached the review-ready objective.
Terminal status after the operator explicitly stopped the monitor.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.supp: Short help below the pull-request URL field naming the four supported hosted products. Keep GitHub.com, GitLab, Azure DevOps Services, and Bitbucket Cloud unchanged.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.term: Label for a machine-readable reason code retained on a finished monitor; the value beside it is intentionally not translated.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.toke: Usage evidence counting input plus output tokens; {{count}} is already locale-formatted or the translated word Unknown, so keep the label before it.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.lega: Note shown on the goal-loop form, which is the popover's default view, beside the offer to watch a pull request instead. It must name the surface the way that panel's own title does (Set a goal), because a reader could not tell that the loop being warned about IS the screen they are on. Explain that each cycle invokes the agent and that the loop can be unlimited.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.set_: Button on the goal-loop form that switches to the bounded monitor form. It must name the SUBJECT, a pull request, because that form accepts nothing else: a label saying only monitor sends a reader with any other goal to a field they cannot fill.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.use_: Button on the bounded monitor form that returns to the goal-loop form, which is the popover's default view. It is a plain return and must NOT warn about cost: a reader refused to press it while it read as a penalty, and it is the only labelled way back. The cost cue lives on the goal form itself, in the warn-coloured legacy_notice. The key name is historical.
entries.components.sessionAutomationPopover.wake: Instructions sent to the agent only after a cheap probe classifies review work as actionable; wake means start an agent invocation.
Inline validation beside the wake-instructions field. {{max}} is an already locale-formatted character limit; preserve the placeholder.
Usage evidence counting distinct actionable events that woke the agent; {{count}} is already locale-formatted, so keep the label before it.
entries.components.chatInput.project_switch_appl: First added line of the composer's project chip tooltip while a response is running. Picking a project then is allowed: the user's next message runs in the picked project, and the response already running finishes in its start project. {{project}} is that start project's folder name, inserted verbatim; keep the placeholder. 'Reply' is one agent response.
entries.components.chatInput.model_switch_applie: Last line of the composer's model chip tooltip while a response is running. Picking a model then is allowed: the pick is committed and the user's next message runs on it, while the response already running finishes on the model it started with. Mirrors components.chatInput.project_switch_applies_next_turn; 'reply' is one agent response.
entries.components.chatInput.project_switch_link: Second added line of the same tooltip, on its own line. File links shown in the running response already open in the project the user just picked, not the one the response runs in; state that plainly.
entries.components.chatInput.project_locked_whil: Tooltip of the project chip while it is disabled because sub-agents are attached to the chat. Says plainly that the project cannot be switched until they finish; no action is offered.
entries.components.chatInput.queue_run_after_the: Description under the Queue option in the busy composer's send menu. 'Current work' can be either a live response or background sub-agents, so do not narrow it to the current turn.
Tooltip for the busy composer's Queue action. It waits until all current work is finished; `Enter` names the keyboard key and must stay verbatim.
entries.components.chatInput.steer_act_on_this_a: Tooltip for the busy composer's Steer action. It injects into a live response, or starts a new response when only background sub-agents are running; translate the broader promise to act as soon as possible. `Enter` names the keyboard key and must stay verbatim.
entries.components.chatInput.steer_act_on_this_r: Description under the Steer option in the busy composer's send menu. It means act on the message now, whether that injects into a live response or starts a new response while background sub-agents continue.
entries.components.chatInput.terminal_run_review: Visible action label and accessible name on the command composer's button. Name both reviewing the command and its terminal destination; this opens a review dialog and does not execute immediately. Keep it brief for narrow composers and distinct from the dialog's final Run button and the palette's Run a command action.
entries.components.chatInput.message_placeholder: Empty local-session composer hint. Keep the message invitation and parenthesized shortcut list in the locale's prescribed tone. Translate shell command after ! as an operating-system shell command, distinct from the /command chat shortcut. Preserve /command, @file, $skill, the separators and the literal space after !; {{bot}} is the bot name.
Empty composer hint in a mate's direct-message thread. Same message invitation as message_placeholder but WITHOUT the parenthesized shortcut list; {{bot}} is the mate's display name, not the product.
entries.components.chatInput.terminal_unavailabl: Notice when the server disables the terminal. Preserve the exact server configuration key dashboard.terminal.enabled verbatim. The final instruction removes the leading literal ! to return to ordinary chat editing; the remaining text can then be sent normally. This edits the draft, does not send automatically, and does not preserve a literal bang. Keep ! unchanged and use the locale's prescribed imperative word order without ending the sentence in !.
entries.components.chatInput.terminal_remote: Refusal for a session hosted by another server; avoid the product jargon remote crew and do not promise a different physical machine. Explain that removing the leading literal ! returns to ordinary chat editing; the remaining text can then be sent normally. This changes the draft, is not a literal-send escape, and does not send automatically. Keep ! unchanged and use the locale's prescribed imperative word order without ending the sentence in !.
entries.components.chatInput.terminal_default_di: Composer status hint when no project is captured, not a label above the confirmation preview: the directory where the server starts the terminal, not the default agent profile. The resolver uses configured cwd, HOME or /; Windows may replace an invalid unrequested default with expanduser('~'). Do not translate this as always home or explicitly configured.
entries.components.chatInput.terminal_force_stop: Compact imperative label beside the force-stop control: stop the agent session, not the terminal command; the button retains its full destructive-action tooltip and accessible name.
entries.components.chatInput.terminal_hint: The terminal panel is the command destination; keep the workspace interpolation without naming a docking position because the panel can be below or beside the chat.
entries.components.chatInput.terminal_panel: Terminal-mode hint when the selected workspace chip already displays its name. The full captured destination remains in the review dialog.
entries.components.chatInput.terminal_review_at_: Tooltip after the terminal tab limit is reached. Review still opens the confirmation dialog; Run then opens the terminal panel. A still-full panel requires closing a tab and a fresh attempt. No command is queued.
entries.components.chatInput.terminal_failed: Compact composer notice after a failed command handoff: the command was not sent, the draft is kept and the user should inspect the terminal panel; name the panel, not a new tab, because a failed redock may not create one.
entries.components.commandPalette.providers.allA: Section heading in Search Everywhere for the aggregated result list that mixes every provider (pages, sessions, skills, prompts…). Means "all categories", not "everything selected".
entries.components.commandPalette.tab: The literal Tab key cap, shown inside a key badge. Do not translate or transliterate: it names a physical key the user presses.
entries.components.crewWakeSection.active: Status word on a schedule row in the crew editor: the job is enabled and will fire. An adjective describing the schedule, not a verb and not "activate". Width-constrained: keep it short.
entries.components.crewWakeSection.new_schedule: Button in the crew editor's schedules pane that expands an inline form to create a new schedule for this crew. "New" is the create action, not a freshness adjective. Width-constrained: keep it short.
entries.components.crewWakeSection.paused: Status word on a schedule row in the crew editor: the job exists but is suspended and will not fire until resumed. An adjective, not the verb "pause". Width-constrained: keep it short.
entries.components.crewWakeSection.running: Status word on a schedule row in the crew editor: a run of this job is in flight right now. An adjective describing the schedule's current state, not a command. Width-constrained: keep it short.
entries.components.crewWebhookSection.last_used_: Timestamp on a webhook token row in the crew editor, {{time}} is an already-localised relative time like '1h ago'. Lower-case: it follows the token's identity on the same line after a separator.
entries.components.crewWebhookSection.off: Badge on a webhook credential row in the crew editor, shown when the credential's admission switch is disabled — the binding exists but cannot call in. 'Off' as in switched off, not 'remove'.
entries.components.crewWebhookSection.retry: Button in the crew editor webhook pane's load-failure box; re-runs the fetch that failed. A verb.
entries.components.discoverySearchBar.no: Answer/state value meaning negative. Not the beginning of a phrase such as "No results".
entries.components.executionsView.ok: Status value in a table or log line, meaning the operation succeeded. A state, not the confirmation button.
entries.components.filePickerMenu.folder: aria-label on the folder ICON in the @-mention picker row and on the staged-folder chip in the composer. A directory in the file system, not a UI grouping.
entries.components.filePickerMenu.folder_kind: Row metadata in the @-mention picker, rendered as 'folder · 3d ago' where a file row shows '12 KB · 3d ago'. Lowercase noun naming the entry kind (a file-system directory).
entries.components.folderColorNames.red: Display name of the red folder color, interpolated into “Set color to {{name}}” on a swatch in the folder-settings color palette. The color adjective as a noun-like label.
entries.components.jobForm.add: Verb on the submit button of the scheduled-job form: add this job. Shown only when the form is horizontal and owns its own submit control, and it swaps to "Adding…" while the request is in flight. If the target language needs an object, name the job.
entries.components.logEntry.ok: Status value in a table or log line, meaning the operation succeeded. A state, not the confirmation button.
entries.components.markdownRenderer.click_to_swi: Hover tooltip on a small inline chip inside chat prose; the chip shows an agent-session identifier and clicking it switches the dashboard to that already-open chat session (an in-app tab switch, not a page navigation). "Session" here is a chat/agent conversation in a developer tool, never a login session.
entries.components.markdownRenderer.session_clos: Hover tooltip on a chat-prose link that names an agent-session which is not open; the link is shown muted and its click does nothing, and this tooltip says why. The session may have closed, or the key may name a session this dashboard never had (a typo'd or foreign sid), so the wording says "not open" rather than "closed". "Session" here is a chat/agent conversation in a developer tool, never a login session; "open" means that conversation is currently available, not a window or a connection. Keep it short — it is a terse status tooltip, not a sentence.
entries.components.markdownRenderer.click_to_sho: Hover tooltip on a small inline chip inside chat prose; the chip shows a chat-sidebar folder path such as goal/worker and clicking it expands and scrolls the sidebar to that folder (a reveal inside the dashboard, not a filesystem directory and not a page navigation).
entries.components.markdownRenderer.image_failed: Status label on the fallback chip for a remote image URL whose bytes failed to load in the chat transcript. A generic load failure, not a statement that the file was deleted.
entries.components.markdownRenderer.image_file_n: Status label on the fallback chip shown when a chat image's LOCAL file is confirmed gone: the load failed AND a follow-up probe of the file endpoint returned 404 (chat images are read from disk at view time; a temp-directory screenshot may be cleaned up later). States a verified fact about the file on disk, not a transient network error.
entries.components.markdownRenderer.format_csv: Short visible word beside the spreadsheet glyph on the copy-actions row under a rendered chat table; a verb label saying the tap copies the table as CSV. Keep "CSV" as the acronym; translate the verb.
entries.components.markdownRenderer.format_markd: Short visible word beside the copy glyph on the copy-actions row under a rendered chat table; a verb label saying the tap copies the table as Markdown. Keep "Markdown" as-is; translate the verb.
entries.components.mcpBrowserModal.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.components.mcpCustomServerModal.env: "env" = environment variables, labelling a key/value editor. An abbreviation of a technical term, not the English word "environment" in its ordinary sense.
entries.components.mcpCustomServerModal.url: "URL", labelling an input field. Lowercase because it matches the config key it edits; do not capitalise or translate.
entries.components.notifications.notificationFee: Filter option meaning no filter — show every item. A quantifier over the list beside it, not the adjective "whole".
entries.components.projectPicker.drive_example_d: A Windows drive-root path (drive letter D, colon, backslash) quoted as the example inside the project picker's "could not show the list of drives" notice, e.g. "...type it above, such as D:\\". A literal path, not a word: keep the letter, colon and backslash as they are.
entries.components.projectPicker.drive_example_e: A Windows drive-root path (drive letter E, colon, backslash) quoted as the example in the same notice when the user is already on drive D, so the example never names the drive on screen. A literal path, not a word: keep it as is.
entries.components.publishHub.kb: The unit "KB" = kilobytes, rendered after a published bundle's size. NOT "knowledge base", which is a separate feature in this product that shares the abbreviation in English.
entries.components.publishHub.checking_for_exist: Muted status line at the top of the Publish panel's destination list while it asks the user's AWS account whether this artifact already has a public web page. The destinations below stay usable meanwhile.
entries.components.publishHub.published_on_publi: Heading of a small card at the top of the Publish panel, shown when this artifact ALREADY has a page on the public internet (published earlier to the user's own AWS account). A state, not an action. The page's URL is shown under it. Use the same word for "published" as the artifact page's "Published artifact" line.
entries.components.publishHub.open_published_pag: Link button on that card. Opens the artifact's already-published public page in a new browser tab. Imperative verb; same wording as the artifact page's link to its published copy.
entries.components.publishHub.update_same_url: Primary button on that card. Publishes the current content again to the SAME public page, so the address does not change. Imperative verb; keep the parenthetical short. "URL" stays as written.
entries.components.publishHub.update_replaces_pu: One line on the publish confirm step when the user chose to update an already-published page. Says the new content replaces what is on that page and the page keeps its web address.
entries.components.publishHub.update_question_le: First word of the question "Update <artifact name> via <destination>?" on the confirm step, when the user is updating an already-published page. Imperative verb, the counterpart of the "Publish" that leads the same question for a first publish. The artifact name and the destination follow it, joined by the "via" word.
entries.components.publishHub.review_update: Button on that confirm step that opens the review of an update of the already-published page. It changes nothing yet: only the later "Confirm & Update" changes the page. Imperative verb.
entries.components.publishHub.confirm_update: Final confirm button for an update of an already-published page, the counterpart of "Confirm & Publish". Translate the same way that string is translated, with the update verb.
entries.components.publishHub.ready_to_update: Words that lead the line "Ready to update <artifact name> via <destination>" on the review step before the final confirm, when the user is updating an already-published page. A state: the update has not started yet, the confirm button sits below.
entries.components.publishHub.existing_link_chec: Title of an error notice at the top of the Publish panel when the panel could not ask the user's AWS accounts whether this artifact already has a public web page. The destinations below it still work.

Second line of that notice. Warns that if the artifact is already published to the public web, publishing from this panel may not update that page (it may create another one instead). Hedged on purpose: say "may not".
entries.components.publishHub.check_again: Button inside that notice that asks the accounts again whether this artifact already has a public web page. Imperative verb.
entries.components.publishHub.update_reviewed_fi: Muted line under the "Update (same URL)" button. Tells the user that pressing it does not change anything yet: a review and a confirm step come first.
entries.components.publishHub.update_ttl_applies: Muted line under the time-limit picker, shown only when updating an already-published page. Says the chosen time limit now governs that page, and that with a limit the page and its web address are deleted when it runs out.
entries.components.publishHub.updating_in_progre: Busy label on the confirm button while an update of an already-published page is in flight. The counterpart of "Publishing…".
entries.pages.artifactDetailPage.published_to_pr: Start of the line "Published to <destination> · Open published page" on an artifact's page. {{provider}} is the destination's display name (for example a personal drive). A state, not an action.
entries.pages.artifactDetailPage.open_published_: Link in the line "Published artifact · <link>" on an artifact's page. Opens the published copy at its destination in a new browser tab. Imperative verb; same wording as the Publish panel's link to a public-web copy.
entries.components.remoteArtifactCard.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.components.runInTerminalConfirm.run: Verb on a button: execute this job/workflow now. NOT the noun ("a run"), which several locales translate differently.
entries.components.runInTerminalConfirm.body_def: No-project composer confirmation for one command line. First state that no workspace is selected, then identify the preview below as the command. No separate destination label appears above it. Resolution uses configured cwd, HOME or /, with an additional Windows home fallback for an invalid unrequested default; do not promise a particular path.

No-project composer confirmation for multiple command lines. First state that no workspace is selected, then identify the preview below as {{lines}} lines, not that many separate commands; preserve {{lines}}. No separate destination label appears above it. Starting directory means configured cwd, HOME or /, with Windows additionally replacing an invalid unrequested default with its home fallback. It is not the agent profile or necessarily home.
entries.components.searchResultsList.you: Speaker label on a search result whose message came from the user rather than the agent — the second-person pronoun as a NAME for the author, the way a chat transcript labels a turn. Not the object "you" in a sentence.
entries.components.selectionToolbar.ask: Button on the floating toolbar that appears over selected chat text, beside Quote and Copy: sends the selection to the Side Chat panel as a question, without touching the main conversation. "Ask" is a VERB, not the noun ("an ask"), and "this" is the selected text. The panel is deliberately NOT named on the button (a first-time reader has not met "Side Chat" yet) — its tooltip, components.selectionToolbar.ask_hint, names it. Sits in a row of short buttons, so keep it brief.
entries.components.selectionToolbar.ask_hint: Tooltip and accessible description of the "Ask about this" toolbar button. One sentence that answers the two first-use worries: the question lands in the Side Chat panel (a separate conversation, so the main chat is not changed) and pressing the button SENDS NOTHING — the selection is only quoted into that panel's composer until the user sends. "Side Chat" is the panel's own name — translate it the same way as pages.chat.sidePanel.menu_side.
entries.components.selectionToolbar.copy: Button on the floating toolbar over selected chat text: copies the selection to the clipboard. A VERB ("copy this"), not the noun "a copy" — several languages use different words for the two. Sits in a row of short buttons, so keep it brief.
entries.components.selectionToolbar.quote: Button on the floating toolbar over selected chat text: inserts the selection into the main composer as a quotation to reply to. A VERB ("quote this"), not the noun "a quote" and not a price quotation. Sits in a row of short buttons, so keep it brief.
entries.components.selectionToolbar.quote_hint: Tooltip and accessible description of the "Quote" toolbar button, the counterpart of components.selectionToolbar.ask_hint: says the selection is quoted into THIS conversation's composer and that the reply therefore goes to the main chat (as opposed to Ask, which opens the Side Chat). One sentence, informal register.
entries.components.sessionActionsMenu.pin: Verb on a menu item that pins the session to the top of the sidebar. Paired with "Unpin" on the same item, which is why it is a bare verb rather than "Pin session".
entries.components.shortcutsModal.global_hotkey_: Help text under the desktop app's system-wide summon shortcut. `globalHotkey` is a literal JSON config key and `Connection > Open Config File` is a literal (untranslated) menu path in the desktop app — leave both exactly as written.

Help text under the summon shortcut when it is OFF — either never set or set but unable to bind — telling the user how to set or change it. `globalHotkey` is a literal JSON config key and `Connection > Open Config File` is a literal (untranslated) menu path in the desktop app — leave both exactly as written.

Shown in the key-cap slot of the summon-shortcut row when the system-wide hotkey is disabled (no key bound), in place of a key combo. Translate as the short adjective for a feature being turned off / disabled.
entries.components.shortcutsModal.show_or_focus_: Label for the OS-level shortcut that brings the Kiro Crew desktop window to the front from any application. 'Kiro Crew' is the product name — do not translate.
entries.components.themeEditor.var_aim: Row label in the theme editor for the `--aim` colour token. AIM is this project's name for the agent-activity accent — an opaque token name, not the English word "aim". Keep it verbatim in every language.
entries.components.themeEditor.var_ok: Row label in the theme editor for the `--ok` colour token: the success/healthy colour, shown beside Warning, Danger and Info. Names the colour role, not an acknowledgement — many languages keep "OK".
entries.components.trustDropdown.trust_all_base: Menu item granting standing permission for a whole command family. {{base}} is one or more command names joined by ', ' and must stay inside the <mono> tag. Middle of three trust options: wider than trust_this_command, narrower than trust_all_tools.
entries.components.trustDropdown.trust_all_tools: Menu item on the chat surface's approval card granting standing permission for EVERY tool, not just the one being asked about. Widest of the three trust options, so it must read broader than trust_this_command and trust_all_base. It must also name its SCOPE: the grant covers this chat session only and is not saved to disk, which is what separates it from trust_all_tools_channel. A reader who cannot see the scope reads "all tools" as permanent and refuses the control.

Menu item on the channels page's approval card, replacing the chat surface's session-scoped 'Trust all tools': this grant covers every agent in the channel and is saved to disk, so it survives restarts. The label must convey both the channel-wide scope and the persistence.
entries.components.trustDropdown.trust_this_comm: Menu item granting standing permission for ONE exact command. {{cmd}} is shown verbatim, already shortened when long, and must stay inside the <mono> tag. Narrowest of the three trust options.
entries.components.voiceDictationPanel.esc_to_ca: Keyboard hint in the corner of the voice dictation panel for BATCH speech-to-text: the user must click the mic to stop and transcribe. 'Esc' is a physical key name. Width-constrained: keep it short.

Keyboard hint in the corner of the voice dictation panel when 'Send when I stop recording' is on, for batch and streaming speech-to-text alike: clicking the mic stops, transcribes and sends the message, and Shift-click stops but keeps the text unsent in the message box. 'Shift' is the keyboard key, written as this locale names it on keyboards. 'Esc' is a physical key name. Width-constrained: keep it short.

Keyboard hint in the corner of the voice dictation panel. 'Esc' and 'Enter' are physical key names -- use the conventional key names printed on keyboards for this locale. Width-constrained: keep it short.
entries.components.voiceDictationPanel.listening: Status label on the voice dictation panel while the microphone is capturing. Present participle describing the app's current state, not a command to the user.
entries.hooks.usePanelTabs.git: Tab label for the Git side-panel view in the chat right panel. "Git" is the version-control tool's proper name - do not translate.
entries.lib.effort.low: Reasoning-effort level in the chat model picker: the least thinking time, fastest answers. An adjective naming an amount of effort, not a volume or a priority.
entries.lib.effort.max: Reasoning-effort level in the chat model picker: the highest setting the model offers. Short for "maximum" — the top of a scale, not a verb.
entries.lib.scriptLabel.latin: Names the writing system of one refused letter, shown in parentheses beside it with its code point, e.g. (Latin letter, U+00E9). A standalone noun phrase in the nominative, because it is inserted as is into the paper-name and namespace-name refusals.
entries.lib.scriptLabel.other: Label for a refused letter from a script with no label of its own, shown in parentheses beside it with its code point, e.g. (character, U+8BBA). A NOUN meaning one written character, not a person's character or a role.
entries.lib.sttProviders.downloading_decoder: Progress line on the Voice settings page while the audio decoder (ffmpeg) is being fetched. Deliberately a separate key from the speech-model bar beside it, because both transfers can run at once and each has to name what it is downloading.
entries.pages.appDetailPage.github_stars: aria-label on the star icon beside the abbreviated GitHub stargazer count in the app detail page's hero subtitle. GitHub repository stars, not a rating.
entries.pages.appDetailPage.github_stars_2: Row label in the app detail page's Details metadata card, with the exact stargazer count interpolated as {{value}}. GitHub repository stars, not a rating.
entries.pages.appDetailPage.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.pages.appsPage.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.pages.artifactDeployPage.aws: The literal name of the AWS CLI executable, `aws`. Do not translate: the user types it.
entries.pages.artifactDetailPage.copy_failed: Brief error status on the artifact content copy button after a clipboard write fails. A past outcome, not a command.
entries.pages.artifactDetailPage.tag_2: Noun: a label attached to an artifact. Not the verb.
entries.pages.artifactDetailPage.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.pages.artifactsPage.all: Filter option meaning no filter — show every item. A quantifier over the list beside it, not the adjective "whole".
entries.pages.artifactsPage.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.pages.artifactsPage.ver: Column header abbreviating "version" in the artifacts table. Abbreviated for column width, not for style.
entries.pages.channelPage.add: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.pages.channelPage.listen_all: Badge on a Slack/Discord channel meaning the agent listens to EVERY message in it. Contrasts with the sibling badges 'mention' (only when @-mentioned) and 'silent' (never). Short, sits next to an icon — keep it to one or two words.
entries.pages.chat.activityViewer.resource_type_: "PR" = pull request. Keep the abbreviation the target language's developers actually use; do not expand it if that would break the layout.
entries.pages.chat.assistantMessage.fork_earlier: Entry in an assistant reply's More menu, listed beside "Fork with later messages only" while the Tail-only Fork setting is on; it makes a new chat that keeps the messages before this one, and the current chat is left as it was. Mirror the sibling entry's phrasing, saying "earlier" where it says "later". "Fork" means branch a conversation, NOT a git branch.

Second line under "Fork with earlier messages" in an assistant reply's More menu. It opens "Starts a new chat with", says which messages the new chat holds (this message and the ones before it), and that the chat the reader is in is left as it was. "Fork" means branch a conversation, NOT a git branch. It sits under the label at small size, so keep it as short as the target language allows. Mirror the sibling hint's phrasing.
entries.pages.chat.assistantMessage.fork_later_m: Entry in an assistant reply's More menu while the Tail-only Fork setting is on, listed above "Fork with earlier messages". It makes a new chat that holds ONLY the messages after this one: not this message and not the ones before it. Name what the new chat holds, mirroring the sibling's "Fork with earlier messages" ("later" where it says "earlier", plus "only"). "Fork" means branch a conversation, NOT a git branch.

Second line under "Fork with later messages only" in an assistant reply's More menu. It opens with "Leaves out this message", so the reader learns first that this message is not copied, then says only the later messages go to a new chat and that the chat the reader is in is left as it was. "Fork" means branch a conversation, NOT a git branch. It sits under the label at small size, so keep it as short as the target language allows. Mirror the sibling hint's phrasing.
entries.pages.chat.assistantMessage.fork_no_late: Replaces the second line under "Fork with later messages only" on the newest message, where nothing follows yet, and the entry cannot be chosen. It says why: no message comes after this one so far. Small text under the label, so keep it short.
