entries.pages.chat.assistantMessage.fork_in_prog: Replaces the label of the fork entry the reader just chose in an assistant reply's More menu, while that fork is being created. Used for both "Fork with earlier messages" and "Fork with later messages only". "Fork" means branch a conversation, NOT a git branch. Keep the trailing ellipsis.
entries.pages.chat.assistantMessage.fork_other_i: Replaces the second line under the OTHER fork entry in an assistant reply's More menu while the chosen fork is being created, saying why this entry cannot be chosen right now. "Fork" means branch a conversation, NOT a git branch. Small text under the label, so keep it short.
entries.pages.chat.decisionStrip.rate_jev: Visible label on the thumbs-up/thumbs-down pair in the transcript decision strip, naming which side that pair rates: Jev's pick, as opposed to the word-match pair beside it. The decision model's product name, so it stays in Latin script in every language; it is not the English word "jev" and it abbreviates nothing. Width-constrained — it sits at the end of a one-line strip that truncates, so keep it as short as the target language allows.
entries.pages.chat.decisionStrip.jev_label: Row label in the transcript decision strip naming Jev, the decision model, as the side that made this pick — paired with the "Word matching" label above it. A product name, so it stays in Latin script in every language; it abbreviates nothing.
entries.pages.chat.pinnedPrompt.collapse_pinned_: Accessible label on the pinned banner's collapse chevron in the chat transcript, shown while the banner is expanded. "Turn" means one conversation turn — the pinned opener is always a prompt the user typed; auto-nudge cycles and subagent completion events are never pinned — not a game move or a waiting-line turn.
entries.pages.chat.pinnedPrompt.expand_pinned_pr: Accessible label on the pinned banner's expand chevron in the chat transcript, shown while the banner is collapsed to its preview. "Turn" means one conversation turn — the pinned opener is always a prompt the user typed; auto-nudge cycles and subagent completion events are never pinned — not a game move or a waiting-line turn.
entries.pages.chat.pinnedPrompt.jump_to_this_tur: Tooltip on the pinned banner's jump button in the chat transcript. "Turn" means one conversation turn — the pinned opener is always a prompt the user typed; auto-nudge cycles and subagent completion events are never pinned — not a game move or a waiting-line turn.
entries.pages.chat.pins.you: Attribution label shown below a pinned chat message indicating which user pinned it. "You" means the current user pinned this message themselves.
entries.pages.chat.thread.you: Author name above the user's own bubbles in a reply thread on a mate chat message (the Crew Members page's thread panel): the second-person pronoun as a NAME for the author, as a chat transcript labels a turn, paired with the mate's name on its bubbles. Not the object "you" in a sentence.
entries.pages.chat.sessionFlyout.new: Label on the small ACTION BUTTON that starts a new chat session, in the recents flyout that opens on hovering the collapsed session sidebar's toggle. Space is tight (the button sits beside a caption in a ~244px panel), so this is the clipped form of the sibling key `new_chat` ("New chat") - translate it as an imperative button, the sense of 'start a new one', not the adjective 'recently made'. If your language cannot shorten it, reuse the `new_chat` wording; a wrapped button beats a wrong sense.
entries.pages.chat.sidePanel.menu_git: Menu entry in the side panel "+" menu that opens the Git view. "Git" is the version-control tool's proper name - do not translate.
entries.pages.chat.toolCallLine.tip_cut_hint: Muted note at the end of the hover bubble over a folded tool step in the chat transcript, shown only when the bubble had to cut a long command or title short. It tells the reader that opening (clicking) the step shows the whole text. "Step" is the tool row in the transcript, the same word as in the other tool-step strings. Keep it short; it follows an ellipsis on one line.
entries.pages.chat.toolDetails.raw: Segment label on the tool-call details panel, paired with "Formatted". Selects the unprocessed payload -- the exact bytes the agent sent or received, with escape sequences left as written -- rather than the prettified table view. "Raw" as in unprocessed data, not uncooked food. Keep it to one short word if the language allows; it sits in a two-segment toggle.
entries.pages.chat.transientNotice.resuming: Warning-tone chat notice shown while the product automatically finishes an answer that a dropped connection cut off: part of the answer is already shown above it and the rest is on its way. Sibling of "Connection unstable — retrying…", which re-sends a whole request that got no answer at all; keep the two distinguishable.
entries.pages.chat.transientNotice.interrupted: Muted chat notice that replaces "Connection unstable — retrying…" once the automatic retry has ended without an answer. Past tense: the connection WAS interrupted; it does not say whether anything is still running, and it is not a button or an instruction.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.redirecting_the_r: Tooltip (title attribute) on the muted "Steering…" indicator above a chat message the user redirected into the agent's RUNNING turn, explaining the jargon for first-time users: the redirect was sent but the backend has not yet confirmed the running turn took it. "Turn" means one conversation turn (the agent's current run).
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steering: Muted progress indicator above a chat message the user redirected into the agent's RUNNING turn (a "steer"), shown while the backend has not yet confirmed the redirect. Progressive verb — "steering is in progress" — NOT the noun used elsewhere for "steering files". Sits where the confirmed "Steered into the running turn" badge later appears, so echo that key's verb.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_unsend: Item in the small "…" menu beside the muted "Steering…" indicator on a chat message the user sent into the agent's RUNNING turn while the agent has not read it yet. Choosing it takes the message back so the agent never sees it, like unsending a chat message. Imperative verb, one or two words.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_edit: Item in the same "…" menu as "Unsend": takes the not-yet-read message back and puts its text in the message box, the text field where the user types messages, so the user can change it and send it again. Imperative phrase naming where the text goes: the message box, using the product's usual term for that field. Not the "Edit & Resend" action on ordinary messages.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_queue_inste: Small text button beside the muted "Steering…" indicator, next to the "…" menu that holds "Edit in message box" and "Unsend": takes the not-yet-read message back from the running turn and puts it in the queue, so it is sent after the agent finishes instead of redirecting the current work. "Queue" is the verb (put in the waiting line), the same meaning as the composer's "Queue message" button. Keep it short.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_take_back_m: Accessible name and tooltip of the small "…" menu button beside "Queue instead" on a chat message the agent has not read yet. The menu holds the "Edit in message box" and "Unsend" actions, so the label names both by their verbs alone ("Edit", "Unsend"): imperative verbs joined by "or".
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_unsend_in_f: Muted progress line that replaces the "Steering…" indicator and its controls while the dashboard waits to learn whether the agent dropped the message before reading it. Shown after the user chose "Unsend". It is the in-progress form of the note "You unsent this message": reuse that note's verb. Progressive form.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_edit_in_fli: Muted progress line that replaces the "Steering…" indicator and its controls while the dashboard waits to learn whether the agent dropped the message before reading it. Shown after the user chose "Edit in message box". It is the in-progress form of the note "You moved this message back to your message box": reuse that note's verb and its word for the message box. Progressive form, "it" is the user's message.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_queue_in_fl: Muted progress line that replaces the "Steering…" indicator and its controls while the dashboard waits to learn whether the agent dropped the message before reading it. Shown after the user chose "Queue instead". It is the in-progress form of the note "You moved this message to the queue": reuse that note's verb and its word for the queue. Progressive form, "it" is the user's message.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_retracted_u: Muted one-line note left in the chat transcript where a message used to be, after the user unsent it before the agent read it. The message itself is no longer shown. Past tense, addressed to the user, like "You unsent a message" in chat apps.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_retracted_e: Same muted note as "You unsent this message", for the case where the user took the message back to edit it: its text went back into the message box, the text field where the user types messages. Use the product's usual term for that field. The note is a link-styled button that moves focus to the message box. Past tense, addressed to the user.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_retracted_q: Same muted note as "You unsent this message", for the case where the user moved the message to the queue: it now waits to be sent after the agent finishes. "Queue" is the waiting line of messages, as in the composer's "Queue message" button. Past tense, addressed to the user.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_take_back_b: Muted line under the "Steering…" indicator when taking a message back was refused because another message is still being sent or taken back at that moment. Nothing changed; the user can press the button again. Two short sentences.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_unsend_unsu: Muted error notice under the "Steering…" indicator of a chat message the agent has not read yet. The user picked "Unsend", and the AI agent the chat runs on cannot drop a message it has not read, so the message stays and the agent will read it. "It" is the user's message. Reuse the verb of the "Unsend" menu item and of the note "You unsent this message".
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_edit_unsupp: Muted error notice under the "Steering…" indicator of a chat message the agent has not read yet. The user picked "Edit in message box", and the AI agent the chat runs on cannot drop a message it has not read, so the message stays and the agent will read it. "It" is the user's message. Reuse the wording of the note "You moved this message back to your message box" and that locale's term for the message box.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_queue_unsup: Muted error notice under the "Steering…" indicator of a chat message the agent has not read yet. The user picked "Queue instead", and the AI agent the chat runs on cannot drop a message it has not read, so the message stays and the agent will read it. "It" is the user's message. Reuse the wording of the note "You moved this message to the queue" and that locale's word for the queue.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_unsend_fail: Muted error notice under the "Steering…" indicator of a chat message the agent has not read yet. The user picked "Unsend" and it failed for another reason (for example the request did not reach the server). Nothing changed. "It" is the user's message. Reuse the verb of the "Unsend" menu item. Short.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_edit_failed: Muted error notice under the "Steering…" indicator of a chat message the agent has not read yet. The user picked "Edit in message box" and it failed for another reason (for example the request did not reach the server). Nothing changed. "It" is the user's message. Reuse the wording of the note "You moved this message back to your message box". Short.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_queue_faile: Muted error notice under the "Steering…" indicator of a chat message the agent has not read yet. The user picked "Queue instead" and it failed for another reason (for example the request did not reach the server). Nothing changed. "It" is the user's message. Reuse the wording of the note "You moved this message to the queue". Short.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_unsend_unco: Error notice under the progress line that replaces the "Steering…" indicator while a take-back is pending. The user picked "Unsend" and the request failed before the server confirmed whether the message was removed. Nothing is needed from the user: the row stays pending and updates by itself when the agent reaches the message. "It" is the user's message and "This" is that status on the row. Reuse the verb of the "Unsend" menu item. Two short sentences.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_edit_unconf: Error notice under the progress line that replaces the "Steering…" indicator while a take-back is pending. The user picked "Edit in message box" and the request failed before the server confirmed whether the message went back to the message box. Nothing is needed from the user: the row stays pending and updates by itself when the agent reaches the message. "It" is the user's message and "This" is that status on the row. Reuse the wording of the note "You moved this message back to your message box". Two short sentences.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.steer_queue_uncon: Error notice under the progress line that replaces the "Steering…" indicator while a take-back is pending. The user picked "Queue instead" and the request failed before the server confirmed whether the message moved to the queue. Nothing is needed from the user: the row stays pending and updates by itself when the agent reaches the message. "It" is the user's message and "This" is that status on the row. Reuse the wording of the note "You moved this message to the queue". Two short sentences.
entries.pages.chat.userMessage.turn_ended_before: Muted one-line explanation above a chat message the user tried to redirect into the agent's running turn, shown when that turn ended before the redirect applied and the message therefore runs as its own, separate message afterwards. "Turn" means one conversation turn (the agent's current run), not a game move or a waiting-line turn. Use a state-neutral present tense: at render time the follow-up message may not have executed yet, and the same line is also read later in history.
entries.pages.chat.sideChat.off_record_marker: Small label at the top of the Side Chat composer band (the tinted box where a side question is typed), beside the same icon as the "Ask about this" toolbar button. Two parts split by a middle dot: the panel's own name ("Side Chat" — translate it the same way as pages.chat.sidePanel.menu_side) and a reassurance that text typed here is NOT saved into the main conversation. Keep it to one short line.
entries.pages.chatPage.open_folder: aria-label and tooltip on the folder chip inside a SENT chat message. Clicking opens that directory in the side panel's file tree; {{path}} is the absolute directory path. Mirror the phrasing of pages.chatPage.open_file.
entries.pages.chatPage.side_chat_pane_gone: Error notice above the main chat composer, shown when the user pressed "Ask about this" in a split-view pane and the page could not switch to that pane's session (typically deleted meanwhile). `{{error}}` is the server's message, appended verbatim. "Side Chat" is the panel's own name — translate it the same way as pages.chat.sidePanel.menu_side.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.close_refused_title: Title of an error notice in the sessions sidebar: the server did not close a session, which is still open.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.close_refused: Body of that notice when the server refused because the session is still saving its last turn. {{title}} is the session title. It clears in seconds; closing it again is the retry.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.close_refused_other: Body of that notice for any other failed close (network, permission, server error). {{title}} is the session title.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.close_this_session_onl: Tooltip and accessible name of the X on a session card that has other sessions under it: the X closes only this session, the ones under it stay open.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.close_keeps_children_h: Muted second line under Close session in the row menu of a session card that has other sessions under it: those sessions stay open.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.release_locally: Label, tooltip and accessible name of the X on a session row that was ADOPTED from a connected remote crew (a local copy of a session that lives on another machine). Pressing it removes only this machine's local copy; the real session keeps running on the remote crew, which this machine cannot close. So the control is NOT called "Close" — a close would promise to end the session, which it does not. "Remove from this machine" names exactly what it does: drop the local copy, leave the remote session alone. Translate it as removing the LOCAL copy from THIS computer, NOT as ending or deleting the session itself.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.release_locally_hint: Muted second line under the Remove-from-this-machine item in that row's menu, shown when the peer's name is known. {{peer}} is the display name of the connected remote Kiro Crew instance the session runs on — the same name the row's "On <name>" chip shows. It reassures the user that removing the local copy does not stop the session (it keeps running on that machine) and that the session stays listed under {{peer}} in the sidebar's session list, where it can be opened again — so the action is reversible, not a loss. Do not use the word "crew"; use the peer's display name.

Abbreviation of "process ID" - a number the reader copies into `ps` or `kill`, so keep it as the platform abbreviation rather than expanding it.
entries.pages.settings.aboutPanel.v: The "v" that prefixes a version number, rendered immediately before the digits with no space (`v1.2.3`). Most languages leave this untranslated.
entries.pages.settings.aboutPanel.app_lane_label: Label prefixed to the version badge on the Settings > About card when the installed desktop app and the gateway it is connected to report different versions; short for "application" and names the desktop app lane, as opposed to the "Gateway" lane below it. A noun, not a verb.
entries.pages.settings.chatPanel.dim_inactive_pa: Label on the settings toggle, next to Split View (Session Grid), that fades the split-view panes without keyboard focus. "Pane" is one session panel of the split view; reuse the pane word the locale chose for split_view_session_grid and its description.
Description under the Dim Inactive Panes toggle. "Accent border" is the coloured outline drawn around the focused pane.
entries.pages.settings.chatPanel.pin_last_prompt: Label on the settings toggle that enables the pinned banner in the chat transcript. "Turn" means one conversation turn — the pinned opener is always a prompt the user typed; auto-nudge cycles and subagent completion events are never pinned — not a game move or a waiting-line turn. Reuse the turn word the locale chose for pages.chat.pinnedPrompt.jump_to_this_turn.

Description under the settings toggle that enables the pinned banner. Same "turn" sense as pin_last_prompt: one conversation turn, whose opener is always a prompt the user typed (auto-nudge cycles and subagent completion events are never pinned).
entries.pages.settings.iMessagePanel.service_sms: One of three choices in the iMessage panel's outbound-transport selector (beside "Auto" and "iMessage"), naming the carrier text-message fallback Messages.app uses when the recipient has no Apple account. The protocol name, not a word: nearly every locale keeps the Latin abbreviation `SMS` rather than expanding or transliterating it.
entries.pages.settings.instancesPanel.20h: A preset retention/timeout duration of 20 hours. The number is data; only the unit letter is translatable, and most locales keep `h`.
entries.pages.settings.notificationsPanel.app: "app" as a notification-delivery target, meaning the desktop application itself rather than Slack or Discord.
entries.pages.settings.notificationsPanel.channe: Row label in Settings > Notifications > Sources for the channel that carries a mate's messages from its direct-message thread. 'Mate' is the product's word for an AI agent on the user's crew (reuse the catalog's existing term); 'messages' are what the mate wrote to the user. Noun phrase.
entries.pages.settings.notificationsPanel.catego: Label of the per-category sound row that plays when the agent needs the user to act: a tool-approval prompt OR a question card asking the user to pick an option. Noun phrase; both kinds share one sound, so name both.

Label of the per-category sound row that plays when a conversation hands control back to the user — it finished, or it paused waiting for the user's input. "Handoff" is the moment control passes to the user; it does NOT fire on every model turn while work continues. Noun phrase.

Description under the "Conversation handoffs" sound row. First sentence: when this sound plays, a conversation finishing and handing control back to the user. Avoid wording like "waits for you" or "pauses for your input", which reads like a question. Second sentence: an explicit question the agent asks plays the sibling "Approvals and questions" sound INSTEAD of this one; keep the "instead" so the reader knows this row stays silent for questions. Quote that row's label exactly as this catalog translates pages.settings.notificationsPanel.category_approval, using the locale's quote marks, so the reader can find the row on the page. Keep both sentences so a reader can tell the two rows apart.
entries.hooks.useWebSocket.waiting_for_input: Body of the native desktop toast (opt-in) shown while the user is away when a conversation paused for their input — an explicit question, or a manual step-through waiting for Go. Sibling of "Response ready", which is the body for an ordinary completion.
entries.pages.settings.notificationsPanel.preset: Name of a notification sound preset — a short percussive 'pop'. One of several sound names in a picker; it names the sound, so translate only if the language has a natural onomatopoeia, otherwise keep it.
entries.pages.settings.notificationsPanel.test_s: Button in the Sound settings card that plays a sample of the current fallback notification sound at the current volume. "Test" is the VERB (try it out); phrase as an imperative action like the sibling per-category "Test" buttons. It only plays a tone — no notification is created or delivered, which is why the English says "sound".
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.plugin_in: Link label under the plugin_refused_fix_steps sentence, which asks the user to reinstall the Session Manager plugin from AWS before running the ownership command. Opens AWS's Session Manager plugin install page (docs.aws.amazon.com) in a new tab. Keep 'Session Manager plugin' and 'AWS' as written; phrase it as a short action, like pricing_calculator.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.plugin_re: Link label under the plugin row's next step when the Session Manager plugin is installed but refused and no fix command is known. Opens the pre-flight troubleshooting entry of the 'Remote Crew on EC2' guide (a GitHub docs page) in a new tab. Keep 'Remote Crew on EC2' as written: it is the guide's title. Phrase it as a short action, like plugin_install_page.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.stop_wait: Button shown while a save has not answered. It stops waiting, but does not undo a save the gateway already applied. The instances list is refreshed to show its current state.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.save_stop: Inline status shown after the user stops waiting for a save. It says that the click did not save anything, the typed draft remains in the editable form, and the user can Save again or Cancel.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.source_ec: Compact source badge on a remote crew row. EC2 is the AWS compute service acronym and should stay as the form practitioners use, normally the Latin acronym.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.type_ssm: Compact connection badge on a remote crew row. SSM means AWS Systems Manager Session Manager; keep the acronym form practitioners use.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.type_ssh: Compact connection badge on a remote crew row. SSH is the Secure Shell protocol acronym; keep the acronym form practitioners use.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.credentia: Detail line of the AWS credentials check when the AWS CLI could not find a program by name. Leads with the edit to make, then says why. {{name}} is that program's file name, {{file}} is the AWS config file's usual path (~/.aws/config) and {{command}} is a shell command (which <name>) the user runs on the computer that runs the product, from the account that runs it, since only there does it see the gateway's PATH; {{productName}} is the product's name. Keep all four placeholders as they are. Keep 'AWS CLI', 'PATH' and 'credential_process' exactly as written: PATH is the environment variable, and credential_process is the AWS config setting the user edits.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.aws_cli_r: Error line of the AWS credentials check when the product found an AWS CLI program but did not run it, because its safety check for programs that receive AWS credentials refused it; so the credentials were not checked. The sentence says only that the credentials were not checked: {{diagnosis}}, which follows it, is one already-translated plugin_refused_* sentence ("Found at <path>, but <product> will not run it: <why>") that says where the CLI was found and why the product, not AWS, did not run it.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.plugin_ow: Plain line under the copyable ownership command in the Session Manager plugin check. Says the command runs in a terminal on the computer that runs the product (which can be another computer than the one showing this page), from an administrator account, that sudo asks for that account's password, and that it changes only who owns the plugin's install folder and its files. Keep 'sudo' as written: it is the command's name.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.plugin_re: Plain instructions under the plugin_refused_* error line, shown when a copyable command below them fixes the refusal by making the plugin's install folder owned by the root account. The first sentence asks the user to reinstall the plugin from AWS first unless they installed it from AWS themselves. Keep 'root' and 'AWS' as written: they are an account name and the company.

Error line of the Session Manager plugin check when the plugin is installed but failed the safety check for programs that receive AWS credentials, for a refusal no plugin_refused_* sentence below covers. {{path}} is a file path and {{reason}} is the check's English reason; both are shown as written.

Plain instruction under the plugin_refused_* error line when no copyable command is known for a permission refusal (any account can change the file or a folder above it), or for a refusal with no code. The quoted button name is the Ask the agent button on the error line above; use this locale's components.askAgent.ask_the_agent text.

Plain instruction under plugin_refused_other_owner when no copyable command is known: install a fresh copy of the program with AWS's own installer, because the product runs a copy only when the file and every folder above it belong to root or to the account the product runs as. A folder such as /usr/local/bin can belong to the other account (a Homebrew run by a second account); then an administrator must make root its owner first. 'The guide' is the troubleshooting link shown right under this text. Keep 'root' and '/usr/local/bin' as written.
Plain instruction under plugin_refused_root_gateway: the product is running as the root account, so the fix is to start it from a regular account. Keep 'root' as written.

Plain instruction under plugin_refused_strict_policy: install the plugin where only the root account can change the file and its folders, at a path with no symbolic links. The quoted button name is this locale's components.askAgent.ask_the_agent text. Keep 'root' as written.

Same opening as plugin_refused_found, then why: the plugin file or a folder above it belongs to another user account on that computer (not an AWS account), {{owner}} (its login name, shown as written), with its numeric user ID {{uid}}; the product runs only programs owned by its own account or by the system administrator account, root. Keep 'root' as written: it is an account name.

Same as plugin_refused_other_owner, for an owning account that has no name on the computer that runs the product (which can be another computer than the one showing this page). {{uid}} is its numeric user ID. Keep 'root' as written.
Same opening as plugin_refused_found, then why: the product itself is running as the root account, and it never runs helper programs such as this plugin as root. Keep 'root' as written.

Same opening as plugin_refused_found, then why: the strict safety check for programs that receive AWS credentials is on (KIROCREW_PROVIDER_BIN_STRICT is the environment variable that turns it on; keep it exactly as written), and it accepts only a file and folders that only the root account can change, at a path that goes through no symbolic links. Keep 'root' as written.
Same opening as plugin_refused_found, then why: every account on the computer can change the plugin file or a folder above it.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.source_ec: Hover tooltip / accessible name for the compact EC2 source badge. Keep 'EC2' and 'AWS' as Latin acronyms. The second sentence must agree with remove_warning: Remove only takes the entry off this list, and the EC2 instance keeps running and billing until deleted in AWS.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.stamped_e: Row caption for a crew that carries the EC2 launcher stamp (provisioner_id) but has no matching launch job in this gateway. It must AGREE with source_ec2_hint and remove_warning: the row WAS launched by the EC2 launcher, its instance may still run and bill, and Remove only takes it off this list. The last sentence names the remedy — delete it in the AWS console — and must agree with remove_warning. Keep 'EC2' as a Latin acronym.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.transport: Hover tooltip for the compact SSM connection badge. 'AWS Systems Manager Session Manager' is an AWS product name — keep it in English.
Hover tooltip for the compact SSH connection badge. SSH is the Secure Shell protocol acronym; keep it as-is.
entries.pages.settings.remoteCrewPanel.identity_: Replaces identity_lookup_failed, identity_unknown_no_answer and identity_unknown_no_portal once the user has picked a Kiro identity (including a pick the form kept while they visited another page): the computer's own sign-in still could not be read, and the crew being launched will sign in with the option selected below. Use this locale's usual word for a crew, as in the panel's other strings.
entries.pages.settings.securityPanel.add: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.pages.settings.securityPanel.off: State value meaning disabled. Not the preposition or the adverb.
entries.pages.settings.securityPanel.tailnet_sta: State badge on the Tailnet origin card meaning the setting is disabled, so no tailnet name is in the dashboard origin allow-list. Sits beside "Active" and "Not resolved" as one of four states. The adjective/state, not the preposition or the adverb.
entries.pages.settings.slackPanel.add: Verb on a button: add an entry to the list beside it. If the target language needs an object, name the thing being added.
entries.pages.settings.sttSettings.decoder_agent: The multi-paragraph message pre-filled into the chat composer by "Let Kiro Crew fix it" -- the user reads it and presses send, so it is ordinary prose, addressed to the agent. Keep every path, `SHA-256`, `ffmpeg`, `<data home>/models/ffmpeg/` and `GET /api/stt/status` verbatim: they are literals the agent acts on. Keep the blank lines between paragraphs.
entries.pages.settings.sttSettings.decoder_failu: Substituted into the decoder hand-off prompt in place of a failure code or detail the backend did not supply. A short lower-case phrase meaning "the system said nothing here", read mid-sentence after a colon; not an error of its own.
entries.pages.settings.sttSettings.decoder_fetch: Sentence above the Download decoder button on the Voice settings page. "Digest-verified" means the bytes are checked against a pinned SHA-256 hash; the point of the sentence is that the user does not have to install ffmpeg themselves.
entries.pages.settings.sttSettings.dictation_pan: Label for the toggle in Settings > Voice that switches the recording UI between the animated dictation panel and the thin status bar.
entries.pages.settings.sttSettings.download_deco: Button that starts the ffmpeg fetch on the Voice settings page. "Decoder" is the audio decoder (ffmpeg), not a UI control; "Download" is the VERB. Sits beside the speech model's own "Download now", so keep the two distinguishable.
entries.pages.settings.sttSettings.let_the_agent: Button shown after the decoder download failed. It hands the failure to a chat session by pre-filling the composer -- nothing is sent -- so the verb should read as delegating the repair to the product, not as the user doing it.
entries.pages.settings.sttSettings.show_an_anima: Description under the 'Dictation panel' toggle in Settings > Voice. 'WebGL2' is a technology name and must not be translated. 'reduced motion' refers to the OS accessibility preference.
entries.pages.settings.sttSettings.submit_on_rel: Label of a toggle in Settings > Voice, written in the user's voice like the neighbouring auto-submit toggle. When on, ending a dictation sends the message as soon as the transcript is ready instead of leaving it in the message box.

One-line hint under the 'Send when I stop recording' toggle. 'Stopping' means ending a recording on purpose (letting go of hold-to-talk, or pressing the mic or shortcut again). 'Shift-click the mic' means clicking the microphone button while holding the Shift key; write 'Shift' as this locale names it on keyboards. 'Slide sideways on the phone' is the finger gesture on the phone's hold-to-talk strip. 'Draft' means the text stays unsent in the message box. Cancelling never sends.
entries.components.chatInput.release_to_send: Hold-to-talk button label shown while the finger holds it. Lifting the finger stops recording and sends the message; 'send' is the verb.
entries.components.chatInput.release_to_keep_dra: Hold-to-talk button label shown after the finger slides sideways. Lifting the finger stops recording and leaves the transcript unsent in the message box; 'draft' is that unsent text, not a saved file.
entries.components.chatInput.slide_up_to_cancel_: Hint strip above the phone's hold-to-talk button while it is held. Two gestures: sliding up cancels the recording, sliding sideways keeps the transcript as an unsent draft in the message box. Keep it short; it shares a line with the button.
entries.components.chatInput.stop_and_send: Tooltip and accessible name of the mic button while recording. Clicking stops recording and sends the message; clicking with Shift held stops and keeps the transcript unsent in the message box. 'Shift' is the keyboard key, written as this locale names it on keyboards.
entries.pages.systemPage.live_system_metrics: Subtitle under the System page title. Deliberately carries no refresh interval: the header is page-level while each plane polls at its own rate (Performance 2s, Sessions 5s), so naming one would be wrong for the others.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.category_bg: Value shown in place of the raw backend value 'bg' in the Spend tab's Origin column, and as a row name when Spend is grouped by origin. It stands for EVERY unattended lane at once (cron, heartbeat, task runner, workflow), so it must read as a group and not as one named lane. Sits beside untranslated transport names such as 'dashboard' and 'slack', so keep it short and lower-case.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.category_col: Column header in the Spend tab, and the middle option of its group-by control. It answers WHICH SURFACE OWNS THE SESSION, derived from the session key. The Context tab has its own origin column (surface_col) answering a different question about one turn, so these two labels must not collapse into the same word in your language.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.category_col_tip: Hover text on the Spend tab's Origin column header. Says where the value comes from (the session key) and that all unattended lanes are reported as one bucket. The lane names in brackets are code identifiers and stay verbatim. It also points at the Context tab's Turn surface column; name that tab, because the column is not on this screen.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.max_col: Column header on the latency profiles: the single slowest sample recorded. It is the far end of the tail and often orders of magnitude above p90, which is why the axis beside it is logarithmic.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.min_col: Column header on the latency profiles: the single fastest sample this instrument recorded in the window. It anchors the left end of the log axis, so it is the floor the profile bar is measured from, not a typical value.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.p50_col: Column header on the latency tables: the median, i.e. half the measured samples finished at or below this duration. "p50" is standard percentile notation and is normally kept verbatim.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.p90_col: Column header on the latency tables: the slow tail, i.e. nine in ten measured samples finished at or below this duration. This is the figure a reader checks when something feels slow.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.prior_credits_turns: Sub-line under the 'vs previous period' spend stat: the previous window's totals, e.g. 'credits 500 · turns 50'. 'credits' is the spend unit and 'turns' counts agent turns; both placeholders are pre-formatted numbers. Deliberately label-before-number so the unit words need no plural agreement (the counts can be 1) — keep that order and the middle-dot separator, and use your language's plain label form of each unit.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.surface_col: Column header in the Context tab. It answers WHICH CODE PATH RAN THIS TURN, read from the turn's own record, so its values are finer than the Spend tab's Origin column (an unattended turn reads 'heartbeat' here and 'all background' there) and can include lanes Spend has no bucket for, such as 'monitor' and 'webhook'. Must stay distinguishable from category_col.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.surface_col_tip: Hover text on the Context tab's Turn surface column header. Says where the value comes from (the turn's own row) and that naming a lane here does not move that turn's spend away from the conversation that owns the session. It also points at the Spend tab's Origin column; name that tab, because the column is not on this screen.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.turns_to_compaction: Table cell in the Context tab's 'To 90%' column: the forecast number of agent turns left before the conversation's context reaches 90% and compacts, e.g. '4 turns'. A plural key (the _one form covers the singular): 'turn' is the same unit as the Turns column.
entries.pages.webhooksPage.0_b: Size unit in the Webhooks run detail pane: zero bytes, shown when a run returned no result payload. 'B' abbreviates byte and is not a word.
entries.pages.webhooksPage.run: Noun, not a verb: one recorded execution of an inbound webhook, used as a column heading in the Webhooks run history. Never an instruction to start something.
entries.utils.agentSwitchFeedback.turn_in_flight: Inline notice shown when a model/agent switch is refused because the agent is mid-response (HTTP 409 turn_in_flight): shown by the chat header notice after an Alt+Shift model-cycle shortcut, and under the Mochi settings model selector. 'Turn' means one conversation turn; reuse the turn word the locale chose for pages.chat.pinnedPrompt.jump_to_this_turn.
entries.utils.agentSwitchFeedback.model_deferred: Transient notice (same surface as turn_in_flight) after a model pick made while a response was running: the gateway accepted it with deferred=true. {{model}} is the picked model's id or 'Auto', inserted verbatim; keep the placeholder. Says the pick applies from the next message and the running reply keeps the model it started with.
entries.utils.agentSwitchFeedback.member_needs_n: Transient notice (same surface as turn_in_flight) after the user picks a crewmate in the agent picker of a chat that already has messages, and the gateway refuses (HTTP 409 member_memory_requires_new_conversation). {{name}} is the crewmate's id, inserted verbatim; keep the placeholder. Says the crewmate keeps its own memory, so it can only start a new chat, and that this chat's agent did not change. A button beside it reads utils.agentSwitchFeedback.new_chat_with.
entries.utils.agentSwitchFeedback.new_chat_with: Button on the member_needs_new_chat notice. Creates a new chat that runs the crewmate {{name}} (its id, verbatim; keep the placeholder) and opens it. Keep it short: it sits on one line beside the notice text.
entries.utils.schedulePresets.category_ops: Category heading in the scheduled-job template gallery. Short for "Operations" -- the group of templates that watch deployments, CI and infrastructure health. A NOUN naming the category, not the verb "to operate". Sits in a row of sibling headings, so keep it about as short as the other category names in your language.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.keys_for_account: Section header on the Accounts & credentials pane of AWS Control, over the list of credential keys (AWS profiles) that belong to ONE account; {{name}} is that account's display name. The noun "keys" as in credentials, not keyboard keys.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.move_to: Menu item in a cloud-drive file row's overflow menu (AWS Control). Opens a folder picker to move this one file; the trailing ellipsis signals a dialog follows.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.move_title: Heading of the move-file folder picker dialog (AWS Control cloud drive); {{name}} is the file being moved. Reads as the start of a sentence completed by the destination buttons below it.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.move_root: Destination button in the move-file folder picker (AWS Control cloud drive): the top level of the Files section, outside every folder. "Files" is this locale's name for the section (apps.awsControl.console.section_files).
entries.apps.awsControl.console.move_up: Destination button in the move-file folder picker (AWS Control cloud drive): the PARENT folder of the one the file is in; {{name}} is that parent folder's name. "Up" as in one level up the folder tree.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.move_no_folders: Empty state of the move-file folder picker (AWS Control cloud drive) when the file is at the top level and the current listing has no folders, so there is nowhere to move it.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.move_moving: Progress line in the move-file folder picker (AWS Control cloud drive) while the server copies then deletes the object. The verb "move" in progress, same word as the row's Move action.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.move_moving_pick: Progress line inside the move-file folder picker (AWS Control cloud drive) while a move runs. The second sentence tells the reader that closing the picker leaves the move running; it is not cancelled.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.move_to_busy: Second line under the disabled "Move to folder…" menu item (AWS Control cloud drive) while another file's move is still in flight. Files move one at a time, so the item is disabled until that move lands.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.move_ask_agent: Label of the hand-off link under a refused move inside the move-file folder picker (AWS Control cloud drive). Opens a chat with the agent about this failed move.
entries.apps.awsControl.console.library_add_empt: Empty state of the "Add from Artifacts" picker (AWS Control cloud drive) when the user has NO artifacts at all — distinct from library_add_none, which is a search or filter that matched nothing.
entries.components.markdownCard.raw: Segment label on the Formatted | Raw toggle of a markdown content card in the chat transcript, paired with "Formatted". Selects the verbatim markdown SOURCE (the exact text, unrendered, with an edit affordance) over the rendered view. "Raw" as in unprocessed source, not uncooked food; keep it to one short word, it sits in a two-segment toggle.
entries.components.featurePreviewIntro.gif_badge: Tiny corner badge over a looping animated capture in the Feature Preview "Learn more" dialog (Settings > Developer), marking the picture as an animation rather than a still. The file-format abbreviation GIF; most languages keep it as-is.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.lib_art_failed: One short line under a placeholder icon on an appearance-pack card in the Library tab, shown when the pack installed but its picture could not be drawn (unreadable or malformed art). Two short sentences: what happened, and the one recovery that works — naming the Import button in the SAME words the `lib_import` label uses in this language (minus its “(.json)…” suffix), so the copy and the control share words. The card stays selectable. Must fit three lines in a 72px-wide tile at 10px (about 11 characters per line), so keep both sentences very short and avoid words that would break with a hyphen.
entries.components.avatarBuilder.lib_format_svg: Format badge on an appearance-pack card in the crew avatar builder's Library tab, beside the built-in/custom badge. "SVG" is a file-format acronym, so keep the form practitioners in the target language use (usually the Latin acronym, untranslated) and keep it short — it sits in a compact badge next to Lottie and Sprite.
entries.apps.meetings.meeting.pausing: Pending label on the Pause button while the pause request is waiting on the server; ellipsis conveys in-progress.
entries.apps.meetings.meeting.resuming: Pending label on the Resume button while the unpause request is waiting on the server; ellipsis conveys in-progress.
entries.apps.meetings.broadcastBar.pausedPlaceho: Compose-bar placeholder while the meeting is paused; names the AGENTS as what stopped (pause does not interrupt the humans in the room) and how to get sending back.
entries.apps.meetings.broadcastBar.pausingPlaceh: Compose-bar placeholder while the pause request is still in flight; must not claim the meeting is already paused.
entries.apps.meetings.broadcastBar.resumingPlace: Compose-bar placeholder while the resume request is in flight; must not instruct the user to click Resume again.
entries.apps.meetings.transcript.emptyHintPaused: Empty-transcript hint while the meeting is paused; reassures nothing was discarded without promising live speech.
entries.apps.meetings.meeting.endingReview: Transitional badge and compose placeholder while the End-and-review request is in flight; explains why controls are disabled.
entries.utils.toolCallTitle.build: Tool-call row title in the chat transcript. Verb: compile or bundle the project (a build step), not a building.
entries.utils.toolCallTitle.lint: Tool-call row title in the chat transcript. Verb: run a linter over the code. The loanword is fine where the language's developers say it.
entries.utils.toolCallTitle.print: Tool-call row title in the chat transcript for a lone echo/printf that only writes text to the terminal. Verb, not a printer.
entries.utils.toolCallTitle.git: Tool-call row title. {{sub}} is a git sub-command such as status or diff; it stays in English, as does Git.
entries.utils.toolCallTitle.git_path: Tool-call row title. {{sub}} is a git sub-command such as status or diff (stays in English, as does Git); {{path}} is the file or directory it was run on.
entries.utils.toolCallTitle.request: Tool-call row title for an HTTP call. {{method}} is an HTTP method such as POST (stays in English); {{host}} is the host name that was called.
entries.utils.toolCallTitle.fetch: Tool-call row title. Verb: download a web page or URL from the host {{host}}.
entries.utils.toolCallTitle.mcp_with_arg: Tool-call row title for a generic tool. {{title}} is the tool's display name, {{arg}} its most telling argument. Use the locale's colon.
entries.utils.toolCallTitle.and_more_one: Collapsed tool-call row. {{title}} is another already-rendered title from this same table; {{count}} further actions were folded into this one row.
entries.utils.toolCallTitle.and_more_other: Collapsed tool-call row. {{title}} is another already-rendered title from this same table; {{count}} further actions were folded into this one row.
entries.utils.toolCallTitle.read_range: Tool-call row title for reading part of a file. {{from}} and {{to}} are 1-based line numbers; keep the en dash between them.
entries.utils.toolCallTitle.search_web: Tool-call row title for a web search. {{query}} is the search text, shown inside the locale's quotation marks.
entries.pages.chat.toolRiskBadge.labelled_tier: Whole visible text of the risk badge on a tool card in the chat transcript, e.g. "Jev: risky". {{tier}} is one of the two tier words below. Jev is the decision model's product name, so it stays in Latin script in every language; it is not the English word "jev" and it abbreviates nothing. Width-constrained - the badge sits on one line beside a confidence number and a thumbs pair, so keep it short.
entries.pages.chat.toolRiskBadge.tier_risky: The more severe of two risk words in the tool-card badge: Jev judged the call destructive, credential-touching, sending local data out over the network, or acting outside the workspace. An ASSESSMENT of the call, never a statement that it was blocked - the call ran.
entries.pages.chat.toolRiskBadge.tier_caution: The milder of two risk words in the tool-card badge: Jev judged the call worth the reader's attention but reversible. Reads as an invitation to look, not as a warning that something went wrong.
entries.pages.chat.toolRiskBadge.annotation_titl: Hover tooltip on the tool-card risk badge. It exists to stop the badge being read as a block: the call was approved by the session's own permission setting and ran, and the flag changed nothing about that. Keep the "it still ran" and "changed nothing" claims explicit.
entries.pages.chat.toolRiskBadge.annotation_note: Short visible text on the tool-card risk badge, after the tier word and score. It is the tooltip's key claim made visible: the flag itself neither allowed nor blocked the call (the session's permission setting decided that). Do not say the call ran or was not blocked. Width-constrained - keep it short.
entries.pages.chat.toolRiskBadge.confidence_titl: Hover tooltip on the number beside the tool-card risk badge, e.g. "(0.88)". Same meaning as the decision strip's confidence tooltip.
entries.pages.chat.toolRiskBadge.rate_jev: Visible label on the thumbs-up/thumbs-down pair in the tool-card risk badge, naming whose answer that pair rates: Jev's risk verdict. The decision model's product name, so it stays in Latin script in every language; it abbreviates nothing. Width-constrained - it sits at the end of a one-line badge.
entries.pages.chat.toolRiskBadge.rate_right_jev: Tooltip and accessible name of the thumbs-UP button in the tool-card risk badge: the reader is saying Jev judged this call's risk correctly.
entries.pages.chat.toolRiskBadge.rate_wrong_jev: Tooltip and accessible name of the thumbs-DOWN button in the tool-card risk badge: the reader is saying Jev judged this call's risk incorrectly.
entries.pages.developer.featurePreviewsTab.decis: Label of the SECOND switch in the Decisions (Jev) settings card, under the main one and visible only while it is on. It is a CONSENT, not a preference: it widens what leaves the machine to include tool-call arguments. Jev is the decision model's product name, so it stays in Latin script in every language. Keep it readable as an addition to the switch above ("Also ...").

Description under the tool-argument consent switch. Three claims must survive translation: the extra data sent is the name and arguments of each tool call in a session that auto-approves them; passwords and keys are replaced before sending; and this changes nothing about which tool calls are ALLOWED. Also keep the last sentence's point that it stays off until the reader turns it on, even when the main switch is already on.

Status chip on one row of the decision-point list in the Decisions (Jev) settings card, meaning that point is switched off and Jev is not consulted for it. One of three chips beside "Active" and "Needs consent scope". A state word a readout would use, not a button and not "remove".

Option label in the 'Which judge answers' picker on the Decisions (Jev) settings card. The PRODUCT NAME of the decision service this card sends to, so it stays 'Jev' in every language; it is three letters only because it is a name.
entries.pages.chat.compactionKeep.summary: The compaction card's shadow line: how many of the session's tool calls Jev WOULD have kept. The conditional is load-bearing — nothing was kept, the compaction is unchanged — so keep a would/hypothetical form and do not render it as a description of what happened. Jev is the decision model's product name and stays in Latin script. {{kept}} and {{total}} are already locale-formatted numbers.
entries.pages.chat.compactionKeep.chars_share: Second half of the compaction card's shadow line, after a middle dot: the share of the conversation's characters Jev's keep-set would carry. It is an UPPER BOUND, not the figure — the gateway counts every conversation row the replay admits by role, and the replay then applies row quotas and a character budget on top — so keep the "up to" or the locale's equivalent hedge; dropping it makes the line claim a measurement nobody took. {{percent}} arrives already formatted as a percentage for the locale, so do not add a % sign.
entries.pages.chat.compactionKeep.rate_label: Visible label before the thumbs-up/thumbs-down pair on the compaction line. An INSTRUCTION, not a noun phrase: it asks the reader to rate the estimate the line just gave — how much Jev would have kept — so use the locale's imperative for a UI label. It deliberately does not repeat Jev's name, which the sentence beside it already carries. Keep it short; it sits on one line beside the thumbs.
entries.pages.chat.compactionKeep.rate_right: Tooltip and accessible name of the thumbs-UP button on the compaction line: the reader is saying Jev judged this compaction correctly. Pressing it again takes the verdict back, which the copy does not need to say.
entries.pages.chat.compactionKeep.rate_wrong: Tooltip and accessible name of the thumbs-DOWN button on the compaction line: the reader is saying Jev judged this compaction wrongly.
entries.pages.developer.featurePreviewsTab.decis: Label of the THIRD switch in the Decisions (Jev) settings card, under the tool-argument one and visible only while the main switch is on. It is a CONSENT, not a preference: it widens what leaves the machine to a whole session transcript. Jev stays in Latin script. Keep it readable as an addition to the switches above ("Also ...").

Description under the whole-transcript consent switch. Four claims must survive translation: the extra data is the conversation plus the INPUTS of its tool calls, sent when Kiro Crew compacts a session automatically; tool OUTPUT is never sent, only its character count; passwords and keys are replaced first; and this changes NOTHING about the compaction — it is a measurement whose answer shows as one line on the compaction notice. Also keep the last sentence's point that it stays off until the reader turns it on, even when the switches above are already on.

Plain-words name of the compaction decision point, in the read-only points list on the Decisions (Jev) card, beside the backend identifier compaction.keep. Keep the parenthetical that says it is only measured, because it is the one thing that distinguishes this point from the two that change behaviour.

One line of what the memory-recall decision point decides, in the read-only points list on the Decisions (Jev) card and at the top of that point's panel. Keep the SUBTRACTIVE claim exact: the decision may only drop recalled memories, never add or reorder one, which is what separates it from a decision that changes an answer. Jev is the decision model's product name and stays in Latin script.
entries.pages.chat.compactionKeep.not_scored: Trails the tool-call count on the compaction card's shadow line, and ONLY on a session whose transcript was too long to score whole: it says how many tool calls were never looked at, so the count beside it is not mistaken for the session's total. Keep the parentheses or the locale's equivalent bracketing — it qualifies the number before it, not the whole line. {{count}} arrives already formatted for the locale.
entries.components.notifications.notificationBan: Button on an approval banner card: the verb, go and look at the request in the bell popover; not the noun (a review).
entries.components.notifications.notificationPer: Button in the bell popover hint: the verb, grant the browser permission to show OS notifications.
entries.pages.settings.notificationsPanel.system: Muted status word beside a check mark in Settings: the permission has been granted; a state, not a command.
entries.pages.settings.notificationsPanel.push_t: One-line status under the Push notifications toggle in Settings while the browser subscription is being created; a progress state (the switch is going from off to on), not a command. Keep the trailing ellipsis.

One-line status under the Push notifications toggle in Settings while the browser subscription is being removed; a progress state (the switch is going from on to off), not a command. Keep the trailing ellipsis.
entries.pages.settings.notificationsPanel.push_b: Short line under the disabled Push notifications toggle when the browser has blocked notifications for the site. It only points the reader back to the System notifications row above, which carries the full sentence and the fix; do not repeat that sentence here.
entries.pages.developer.featurePreviewsTab.decis: Status chip on one row of the decision-point list in the Decisions (Jev) settings card, meaning Jev IS consulted for that point. The counterpart of "Off" on the same list, so translate it as the same kind of switch-state word. It says the point is PERMITTED, not that something is happening right now -- a word meaning "running" or "in progress" would be wrong. Not a button.

Line under the read-only address in the Decisions (Jev) settings card, telling the reader where that address is changed. The dashboard deliberately offers no control for it, and the sentence has to leave the reader able to find the file. `decisions.provider.endpoint` and the path are literals: never translate either.
Inline error when the provider settings could not be read (other than an older gateway that has no such route).
Inline error in the decision-model picker when the machine's total memory could not be read. Without it no local model can be marked as recommended; the picker still works.

Warning under the decisions provider picker when config.json names a hand-written loopback address: Kiro Crew sends it no Jev API key, so a local tunnel/proxy to hosted Jev must supply the key itself.

Replaces decisions_egress while the provider is a model server on this machine. Same four categories as decisions_egress, worded identically; the point is that the request goes to a local address and Kiro Crew sends nothing over the internet, while the server itself decides what it does with it.
Heading of the provider picker in the Decisions (Jev) settings card: which model answers decisions.
Under the Decision model heading. Says a local model runs on this machine and that the product downloads and runs it.
Radio option for the hosted provider. 'Jev' and 'TypeSafe' are product names: never translate.
Detail line under the hosted option. '0.7 s' is a measured latency; keep the number.
Picker option that runs no decision model at all; the way to stop a local model.
Detail under the no-model option: nothing leaves the machine and nothing runs.
Shown beside the disabled switch while no decision model is chosen.
Detail line under a local model. {{percent}} and {{hard}} are formatted percentages of Jev's accuracy, overall and on hard decisions.
Detail line under a local model. {{peak}} and {{total}} are formatted memory sizes (e.g. '15GB'): how much the server uses, and the machine size it is recommended for.
Detail line under a local model. {{p50}} and {{p95}} are formatted durations: typical time per decision and the slow tail.
Badge beside the model suited to this machine. {{memory}} is the machine's total memory, formatted (e.g. '32GB').
Badge beside the model currently configured.
Button that switches the provider to the selected model.
Shown once the reader picks a model they have not saved yet. 'Use this model' is the button label.
Fine print under the picker explaining where the accuracy numbers come from. 'JevBench' is a benchmark name and 'CPU' stays as is.
Inline error when switching the provider failed; nothing changed.

Note under a decision-model option the organization's security policy does not allow (capabilities.decisions for hosted Jev, capabilities.decisions_local for a local model). The option cannot be chosen.

Line under the earlier-conversation number box in the Decisions (Jev) settings card. Two facts must survive: the number in the box is a CEILING saved with the reader's consent, and the config file holds a separate value the product asks with, which the ceiling caps. `decisions.history_budget_chars` and the path are literals: never translate either.

Line above the consent switch in a decision point's panel, shown only while that point's row says "Needs your OK". It answers "where do I give it?" by naming the switch directly below, so the reader is not left guessing. Keep the reference to something BELOW the sentence.
entries.components.fileChangeChips.highlighting: Two-word status at the right end of a diff card's title row (beside the filename), shown only while the card's SYNTAX highlighting (colouring of code) is still being computed; it disappears when the coloured rows appear. The sense is syntax colouring, never marking or selecting text. A progressive form with a trailing ellipsis, like the neighbouring computing_line_by_line_diff. Keep it short: it shares one row with the filename.
entries.components.fileRenderers.slides_ask_agen: Small link-styled button on the row that says a slide deck is shown as a text outline because the gateway host has no LibreOffice. Clicking it opens the chat with a pre-filled request to the agent to install LibreOffice; nothing is installed by the click itself. Verb + object.
entries.components.fileRenderers.slides_install_: The message pre-filled into the chat composer by "Ask the agent to install it" -- the user reads it and presses send, so it is ordinary prose addressed to the agent. Keep `LibreOffice` verbatim.

Second paragraph of the same pre-filled message, present only when the gateway sent an install command for its platform. {{hint}} is that command (for example `sudo apt install libreoffice`) and must stay verbatim.
entries.pages.developer.featurePreviewsTab.decis: Under a local model that has not been downloaded yet. {{size}} is a formatted size like '8.4 GB'.
Under a chosen local model, before and while it runs. {{name}} is the model name; {{peak}} a formatted size like '15 GB'. 'No model' is the picker option of that name.
Under a local model whose files are already on this machine. 'Use this model' is the button label.
Button that deletes a downloaded local model to free disk space. {{name}} is the model name, {{size}} a formatted size.
Error shown when deleting a downloaded local model fails.
Progress line while model files download. {{done}} and {{total}} are formatted sizes like '1.2 GB'.
Accessible label of the download progress bar.
Status while the model's Python dependencies are being installed.
Status while the local model server loads and starts.
Under the download or install progress: decisions are skipped meanwhile, and how to stop it. "Use this model" is the button label.
Shown when reading the local model's progress fails; the figure on screen may be stale.
Status once the local model server is answering.
Status line for a local model whose server runs while the Decisions consent switch is off; 'Decisions' names that switch.
Error shown when the local model could not be downloaded, installed or started.
Button that retries downloading and starting the local model.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.remote_o: Question at the bottom of the first-run setup screen in the desktop app, before the remote_only_skip link. It asks whether the user's crews run on another computer (a dev box or server reached over SSH) rather than this one, in which case this computer needs no coding agent and the user can connect to that crew instead. 'Crew' is the product's word for a running Kiro Crew instance.

Link-style button after remote_only_question on the first-run setup screen, followed by an arrow icon. Pressing it opens a form where the user enters the address of a crew on another machine and connects this app to it. It does not skip or remove anything; it is the way forward for users whose crews run elsewhere. An imperative, like a button label.
Error shown under the remote_only_skip link when the desktop app could not open the connection form, the form for connecting to a crew on another machine. The retry is pressing that same link again.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.check_ag: Label of the re-check button inside the first-run setup screen's Kiro CLI card. Same action as the plain "Check again" on that screen's other cards, but named for Kiro CLI because another agent's panel can show its own "Check again" at the same time. "Kiro CLI" is a product name: keep it in Latin script, unchanged.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.could_no: Error notice inside a coding agent's row on the first-run setup screen, beside the "Use <agent>" button whose config save just failed. It names the save as what failed: the row above it can be reporting the same agent installed and ready, and that is still true. The second sentence names the retry control: "Use {{name}}" must be rendered exactly as this locale's use_agent button label, with the same {{name}} placeholder, so the reader can find the button it names.

Error notice under the "Use Kiro CLI instead" button on the first-run setup screen, shown when switching the configured agent back to Kiro CLI failed to save. The second sentence names the retry control: "Use Kiro CLI instead" must be rendered exactly as this locale's use_kiro_cli_instead button label. "Kiro CLI" is a product name: keep it in Latin script, unchanged.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.agent_re: Error notice under a coding agent's row on the first-run setup screen when pressing Check again did not produce an answer. Same vocabulary as the row's 'Check failed' pill (agent_unverified): one check, one failure, said the same way in both places. The second sentence names the retry control: "Check again" must be rendered exactly as this locale's check_again button label in this same kiroPrerequisiteGate namespace. {{name}} is the agent's name.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.could_no: Error notice at the top of the first-run setup screen when the gateway's config could not be read, so the screen does not know which coding agent is selected. "Coding agent" is the same everyday term the rest of this screen uses; do not use the developer term "backend" here.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.sandbox_: Explanation shown under a coding agent's row on the first-run setup screen when the agent is installed but the host's sandbox cannot isolate it. Plain-words sense: the product only lets this agent run inside a sandbox that hides the user's credentials from the agent; the host cannot build that sandbox now, so the agent cannot be used until it can. {{name}} is the agent's name, {{productName}} is the product.

Sibling of sandbox_blocked_agent_detail for a DIFFERENT cause: the host's sandbox works, but the user switched it off in the product's own settings (the config key agent.sandbox, which must stay in English verbatim). Sense: the product only runs this agent inside a sandbox that hides the user's credentials from it; that sandbox is currently turned off by a setting, and turning the setting back on is the only remedy — the host is fine, so nothing about re-checking or diagnosing the host applies. {{name}} is the agent's name, {{productName}} is the product.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.agent_ho: Short status pill beside a coding agent's name in the agent pickers (first-run setup and Settings > Agent Harness), paired with sandbox_blocked_agent_detail. Sense: this computer (the gateway host) is unable to build the sandbox the product runs the agent in; it is a fact about the machine, not a setting. Must name the HOST as the cause and read as clearly different from the sibling pill agent_sandbox_turned_off, whose remedy is the opposite.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.agent_sa: Short status pill beside a coding agent's name in the agent pickers, paired with sandbox_off_agent_detail. Sense: the host CAN sandbox, but the product's sandbox has been switched OFF by the user's own setting; nothing is broken or missing. Must name the deliberate switch-off as the cause and read as clearly different from the sibling pill agent_host_cannot_sandbox, which blames the host.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.agent_un: Short status pill beside a coding agent's name on the first-run setup screen. Sense: the gateway's INSTALL CHECK for this agent did not produce an answer, so the product does not know whether the agent is installed; the detail line below tells the user to press Check again. Not 'never checked' and not 'the agent failed'. Must read as clearly different from the sibling pill 'Installed, not active yet' (agent_restart_needed), which is a POSITIVE install verdict.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.agent_re: Short status pill beside a coding agent's name on the first-run setup screen. Sense: the check CONFIRMED the agent is installed, but the running gateway process has not picked it up yet, so it cannot be used until Check again (or a restart) does. Status only, no instruction: the detail line below carries the remedy. Must read as clearly different from the sibling pill 'Check failed' (agent_unverified), where the install verdict is unknown.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.agent_wr: Short status pill beside a coding agent's name in the agent pickers (first-run setup and Settings > Agent Harness), warning colour. Sense: the agent IS installed on the gateway host, but its release is not the one the product verified, so the product refuses to start it; the detail line below names the release found and the command below that installs the verified one. Status only, no instruction. Must read as clearly different from the sibling pills 'Not installed' (agent_not_installed) and 'Check failed' (agent_unverified).

Detail line under a coding agent's row, paired with the 'Wrong version' pill, directly above a copyable install command. Sense: the gateway host has {{name}} at release {{version}} (a version number such as 1.0.103, never translated); {{productName}} only starts the one release it tested, and this is not it, so the user installs the tested release with the command shown below to use this agent. {{name}} is the agent's name, {{productName}} is the product.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.gateway_: Second half of the small breadcrumb-style eyebrow above the 'Set up Kiro' title on the first-run setup screen ('SETUP -> Gateway host'), shown when the gateway did not name a platform. It replaces the platform-bearing form 'Linux gateway' ('{{platform}} ' + the `gateway` key). 'Gateway host' is the machine the gateway runs on, the same term the rest of this screen uses.
entries.components.kiroPrerequisiteGate.update_k: Helper line directly under the Update Kiro CLI button on the 'Kiro CLI is out of date' setup screen. Sense: pressing the button makes the product itself run the command on the gateway host on the user's behalf, so they do not have to open a terminal. <0>{{command}}</0> wraps the literal shell command (for example kiro-cli update), which is shown in code type and must never be translated; keep the tags around the placeholder.
entries.components.cliPanel.invalid_cwd_message: Terminal error when a requested directory is missing, inaccessible, or cannot be checked in time. Names the requested full path and offers restoring it or explicitly choosing the terminal starting directory.
entries.components.cliPanel.use_starting_directo: Button below the invalid-directory terminal error. Explicitly retries without the refused workspace path, using the server-configured terminal starting directory (not necessarily the home directory); never resends the failed command.

Tooltip on the Use terminal starting directory button. Says where the new shell opens: the server-side terminal directory setting dashboard.terminal.cwd (keep that config key in English verbatim), else the server's home directory. Also says the refused command is not resent.
entries.pages.chat.quoteCard.you: Author label on a quote card (the composer's staged quote and the quote at the top of a sent message) when the quoted message was written by the current user. "You" names the reader as the speaker of the quoted words; the informal second person where the language distinguishes.
entries.pages.chat.quoteCard.assistant: Author label on a quote card when the quoted message was written by the assistant: the product name the surface already uses for it ("Message Kiro Crew…"); a mate DM shows the mate's name instead of this label.
entries.components.markdownPanel.open_in_app: Row in the file viewer's ⋯ menu that opens the file being viewed inside another dashboard app, in that app's own window; {{app}} is that app's sidebar name (today the Files app, so the row reads "Open in Files"). A menu label, so no trailing full stop.
entries.apps.fileExplorer.fileExplorerPage.link_: Title of the error notice on the Files page when a link into it (another surface's "Open in Files") named a path the page could not open; {{path}} is the path the link named, shown verbatim. The reason follows on its own line.

Dismissable status banner (not an error: nothing was requested) on the Files page when a link into it named a relative path, which the page refuses before asking the server; {{path}} is the path the link named, shown verbatim. States what happened and the constraint (links need a full, i.e. absolute, path) without telling the reader to do anything, since someone who clicked a link cannot edit it.
entries.pages.settings.displayPanel.terminal_cur: One of three terminal cursor-shape options (Block / Bar / Underline) in a settings button group. "Bar" is a thin vertical I-beam caret shape, not a toolbar or a measure; translate it as the slim vertical text cursor.
entries.pages.settings.aboutPanel.update_refused: Settings > About update dialog error when Update was refused because the git checkout has local edits; {{changed}} is the number of changed files. 'Update now' is the dialog's button label, and the last sentence points at a git stash command shown beneath it. {{productName}} is the product name.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.crew_status_disabled: Status word beside a remote crew's name in the sidebar when its owner has switched that crew off (no connection is opened); the state, not an action button.
entries.uiLocations.description.chat_model_picke: Never shown on screen: the assistant's find_ui tool quotes it to describe the composer's model chip, whose own label is the session's model name. Describe the control; do not invent a label.
entries.uiLocations.description.chat_memory_mode: Never shown on screen: the assistant's find_ui tool quotes it to describe the memory-mode chip, whose own label changes with the mode (incognito, temporary, persistent). Describe the control; do not invent a label.
entries.uiLocations.description.chat_session_tit: Never shown on screen: the assistant's find_ui tool quotes it to describe the session title in the chat header, whose own label is the session's name. Describe the control; do not invent a label.
entries.uiLocations.description.composer_approva: Never shown on screen: the assistant's find_ui tool quotes it to describe the composer's approval-mode picker, whose own label is the current mode (Normal, Reads, Trust or YOLO). Describe the control; do not invent a label.
entries.uiLocations.description.composer_voice_i: Never shown on screen: the assistant's find_ui tool quotes it to describe the composer's microphone button, whose own label changes with what a press does (start or stop recording, transcribing, switch to voice or keyboard). Describe the control; do not invent a label.
entries.components.guideLayer.role_button: Guide panel: the kind of control (“button”) appended to a candidate in the list the person picks from when several controls share a name, e.g. “Main navigation · button”.
entries.components.guideLayer.role_link: Guide panel: the kind of control (“link”) appended to a candidate in the list the person picks from when several controls share a name, e.g. “Main navigation · link”.
entries.components.guideLayer.role_tab: Guide panel: the kind of control (“tab”) appended to a candidate in the list the person picks from when several controls share a name, e.g. “Main navigation · tab”.
entries.components.guideLayer.role_menuitem: Guide panel: the kind of control (“menu item”) appended to a candidate in the list the person picks from when several controls share a name, e.g. “Main navigation · menu item”.
entries.components.guideLayer.role_switch: Guide panel: the kind of control (“switch”) appended to a candidate in the list the person picks from when several controls share a name, e.g. “Main navigation · switch”.
entries.components.guideLayer.role_checkbox: Guide panel: the kind of control (“checkbox”) appended to a candidate in the list the person picks from when several controls share a name, e.g. “Main navigation · checkbox”.
entries.components.guideLayer.role_textbox: Guide panel: the kind of control (“text field”) appended to a candidate in the list the person picks from when several controls share a name, e.g. “Main navigation · text field”.
entries.components.guideLayer.role_option: Guide panel: the kind of control (“option”) appended to a candidate in the list the person picks from when several controls share a name, e.g. “Main navigation · option”.
entries.components.guideLayer.role_combobox: Guide panel: the kind of control (“drop-down”) appended to a candidate in the list the person picks from when several controls share a name, e.g. “Main navigation · drop-down”.
