entries.components.guideLayer.step_caution: Guide panel line shown under the instruction when the highlighted control deletes or removes something (Delete, Uninstall, Clear all). It warns that what the control removes cannot be restored, and that the guide only points: pressing the control is still the person's own act.
entries.components.guideLayer.step_page_open: Guide panel instruction while the person is not on the page a guide is for: the highlighted control is the menu entry (or tab) that opens that page; {{target}} is the page's name as the dashboard shows it. The guide does not open the page itself.
entries.components.guideLayer.step_page_here: Guide panel line once the person is on the page the guide was for; {{label}} is the page's name. Nothing else is highlighted, so it tells them they have arrived and that Done closes the guide.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_tickjob: Guide panel line on the Schedule page's job list when the guide moves ONE job to a folder: the person ticks that job's checkbox and no other, because the folder button moves every ticked job.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_app: Guide panel line on the Library page's grid of app cards: the person opens the ⋯ (More actions) menu on the card of the app the guide is about; clicking the card itself opens the app instead.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_empty_app: Guide panel blocker on the Library page when no app is installed, so there is no app card to choose.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_confirm_app: Guide panel line when an app card's ⋯ menu was already open as the step began: the person may open another app's menu instead, or press Next to go on with this one.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_confirm_uns: Same as select_confirm_app, for when the person has not seen the list unpicked: Next goes on with the app whose menu is open.
entries.pages.libraryPage.installed_apps: Accessible name of the Library page's grid of installed-app cards (read by screen readers; a guide points at it as the list to choose an app from).
entries.components.guideLayer.predicate_no_respo: Guide panel blocker on the chat's model button: it is disabled while the chat is answering, so the person waits for the answer or stops it before the guide can point at it.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_open_named: Guide panel line under the confirm before a step that removes something; {{name}} is the exact name of the session, mate or job open on the page, so the person sees which one the removal is about.
entries.components.guideLayer.predicate_has_sche: Guide panel blocker: what the person must do first because the Schedule page has no jobs yet, so the job table (and its Select all box) is not drawn. Completes a sentence like “To get there, …”, so it starts in lower case.
entries.components.guideLayer.find_nothing_yet: Guide panel line when the control the guide looks for is drawn only while there is something for it to act on (Clear all with no notifications) and it is absent. Says there is nothing for it to do right now, instead of asking to open a menu.
entries.components.guideLayer.step_target_disabl: Guide panel instruction when the highlighted control is disabled (greyed out), so pressing it would do nothing; Done closes the guide. Done names the guide panel's own Done button.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_the_only_on: Guide panel instruction on a choose-one step when the list holds exactly one item (often one scheduled job on a phone): names that item and says the guide continues once it is open.
entries.components.guideLayer.predicate_mouse_in: Guide panel blocker on the chat box's "+" menu: the menu is drawn only for a mouse or trackpad, so on a touchscreen the step cannot point at it.
entries.components.guideLayer.predicate_phone_co: Guide panel blocker on Connect your phone: the rail draws that button only where pairing a phone is available, so the guide says so instead of pointing.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_artifact: Guide panel line on the Artifacts library: the person opens (clicks) the artifact the guide is about; its own page then continues the guide.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_empty_artif: Guide blocker when the Artifacts library is empty, so no artifact can be chosen.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_confirm_art: Guide confirm line when an artifact's page is already open: Next goes on with it; opening another one changes the choice.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_confirm_uns: Same as select_confirm_artifact, for when the library is not on screen: Next goes on with the open artifact.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_pick_named: Guide panel line on a choose-one step when the person named the item: names it as the page shows it (a translated app name), since the question may have used another name.
entries.components.guideLayer.predicate_goal_loo: Guide blocker before the goal button: no goal loop (auto-nudge) runs in the open chat, so its Pause is not there.
entries.components.guideLayer.predicate_monitor_: Guide blocker before the goal button: no unfinished monitor watches the open chat, so its Stop monitor is not there.
entries.components.guideLayer.select_the_only_on: Guide panel line on a choose-one step whose pick is the row's checkbox (the outline is on that checkbox) when the list holds exactly one job.
Guide panel line on the Library's choose-the-app step when only one app card is listed: the outline is on that card's ⋯ (More actions) button.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.bulk_switch_keeps_conv: Description under the Switch All Sessions heading, where one model is picked for every live session. The conversation itself (the transcript and the agent's memory of it) is kept and resumes on the new model, so do not word it as a reset, a deletion or a fresh start.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.bulk_switch_stops_runn: Red caveat in the Switch All Sessions panel, shown only after the user unticks the 'Skip N running sessions' checkbox while some sessions are mid-reply: those sessions are switched as well, and the reply each is producing is cut off.
entries.components.markdownRenderer.closed_sessi: Short one-line inline error shown right beside a chip or link in chat prose that names an earlier (closed) chat session, after the reader clicked it and the app could not check whether that session still exists. {{name}} is the session identifier the chip or link names (for example chat-7-1791000000), shown verbatim; keep it short so it fits on one line. 'Session' is a chat/agent conversation in a developer tool, never a login session.
Button label beside that inline error; clicking it checks again and opens the earlier chat session if it is there.
entries.pages.overview.usageTab.spend_over_time: Title of the Usage tab card holding the stacked area chart of credits spent per day over the last month. "Spend" is the noun (money/credits consumed), the same word the Billing card uses for its "Spend" row in this locale. The bracketed unit names what the chart's numbers are, so a reader does not take them for money; reuse the Billing card's word for credits and your locale's bracketing.
entries.pages.overview.usageTab.harness_unread: Error notice shown in place of the Spend over time card when the dashboard could not read the agent backend setting (the request failed, nothing cached); a Try again button sits under it. The chart stacks credits, which only some backends bill in, so without that setting it cannot tell whether to show at all; the notice says that and no more. "Agent backend" is the Developer tab's term for the harness (kiro-cli, KAS, Claude Code); reuse that tab's word for it, and the Usage tab's word for credits.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.layer_by: Label before the dropdown that chooses which dimension the stacked chart is split into (channel, agent, model, session start week). "Layer" is the verb: divide the stack into layers by this.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.by_chann: Dropdown option: split the chart by the channel each session came from -- dashboard chat, cron, background jobs, a messaging transport such as Telegram or Slack. The same sense as the Spend panel's channel column; reuse that word.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.by_agent: Dropdown option: split the chart by the agent that ran each turn. The noun as in the Sessions table's Agent column.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.by_model: Dropdown option: split the chart by the language model that served each turn.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.by_cohor: Dropdown option: split the chart by the week in which each session was first seen, so long-lived sessions and new ones are separate layers. Plain words, not the statistical term "cohort"; the week is when the session STARTED (first appeared), not the week the spend happened.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.cumulati: Label beside the switch that turns the chart into a running total, so each layer's height is everything that bucket has spent so far rather than that day alone. The adjective describing the view.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.other: Legend label for the layer that folds every small bucket past the top few into one. {{n}} is how many buckets were folded, already locale-formatted; "more" tells the reader it is a count of further groups, not a value. Keep the parentheses or your locale's equivalent bracketing.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.unattrib: Legend label for the layer of turns whose session key, agent or model was never recorded. It is not an error and not a bucket named Unknown by a user; the adjective meaning "not assigned to any bucket".

One-line caption shown under the controls whenever the chart has an Unattributed layer, so the reader learns what it holds without hovering. Starts with the same word as the Unattributed legend label, then a short explanation: these are turns that did not record the detail the chart is split by (agent, model, or session). Must fit any of the three dimensions.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.channel_: Legend label, in the channel view, for sessions whose key is not a recognised channel shape (not dashboard, cron, a messaging transport, ...). Keep it distinct from the "Other (n more)" fold label, which is a different layer.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.cohort_w: Legend label for one layer when splitting by session start week: the ISO week starting on the Monday {{date}}, which arrives already locale-formatted as a short month-and-day (e.g. Sep 7). The caption above the chart explains that a layer is the sessions first seen that week, so this stays short: it sits in a legend next to a number.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.cohort_s: Legend label for the OLDEST layer drawn when splitting by session start week. A cohort is the week a session was first seen inside the 30-day window, so the oldest layer also holds sessions that began before the window; it is named for the last day those sessions could have started by, not as a week of starts: {{date}} is the Sunday closing that week (or the window's last day when the week is still running), formatted as a short month and day. Reads as "started on or before {{date}}"; keep it short, it sits in a legend beside the "Week of" labels.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.cohort_c: One-sentence caption shown under the controls while the chart is split by session start week. States the rule (a session's week is the week it was FIRST SEEN inside the 30-day window, not when it truly began) and its consequence: a session that began before the window counts from its first turn inside it, so the oldest layer -- the one carrying the cohort_started_by label, quoted here without its date -- also holds older sessions. Quote the same words your cohort_started_by translation uses, in your locale's quotation marks; where the date comes first in your label, an ellipsis may stand for it.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.total_to: First line of the chart's hover tooltip in the cumulative view: everything spent from the start of the window up to and including the hovered day. {{value}} is the already-formatted number; place it where your language wants it.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.total_th: First line of the chart's hover tooltip in the per-day view: what was spent on the hovered day alone. {{value}} is the already-formatted number; place it where your language wants it.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.empty: Shown in place of the chart when no spend has been recorded in the window. A plain state, not an error.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.truncate: Warning caption shown under the controls when the server kept only the newest turns of the window because there were too many to retain; {{n}} is how many of the oldest were left out, already locale-formatted. Leads with the consequence (the totals on screen are lower than the true spend), then says why. A warning about the numbers, not an error.

The same warning caption as truncated_notice, used when the server can also name the first day it kept whole: {{n}} is how many of the oldest turns were left out and {{date}} the first day whose turns are all counted, both already locale-formatted. Same lead (the totals on screen are lower than the true spend), then the dropped count, then that every day from {{date}} on counts all of its turns -- say it per day, not "the chart is complete", because a running total from that day still misses the dropped turns. Days before {{date}} may be partly or wholly missing.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.load_fai: Bold title of the error box shown in place of the chart when the first request for the series fails (the raw error text follows it). Says which thing could not be loaded -- the spend-over-time chart -- in the past tense of an attempt that failed, like the other Couldn't load titles in this locale.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.retry: Button under that error box that asks for the series again. Short imperative; reuse your locale's usual Try again / Retry button label.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.loading: Short status word shown beside the Layer by dropdown while a newly chosen dimension is still loading and the previous dimension's chart stays on screen dimmed. Your locale's usual Loading… label with its ellipsis.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.aria_lab: Accessible name of the chart image for screen readers: a stacked area chart (layers of area stacked on top of each other) of spend over time.
entries.pages.overview.usageSeriesChart.keyboard: Appended to the chart's accessible name for screen-reader and keyboard users: the plot can be focused and the left/right arrow keys move the highlighted day (whose values the tooltip then reads out). One short imperative sentence.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.running_marker: Accessible name and tooltip of the small pulsing dot in front of a session's name in the sidebar list, shown while that session is working (the agent is replying, running tools, or has sub-agents running). A state word meaning "currently in progress", not a command to run something; keep it as short as the language allows.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.chat_with_folder: Label of the control that opens a sidebar folder's own chat: the folder row's chat button (its tooltip, accessible name and hover label) and the first item in the folder's actions menu. {{folder}} is the FOLDER's own name, shown verbatim. It names the folder the reader is pointing at, not the chat's title. Keep it a short 'talk to this' label with no word for folder: the reader is already on the folder row.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.conductor_tag: Small tag beside the agent name on the one card a sidebar folder is drawn around: the chat that started the folder's other chats. It is a role that chat plays in that folder, not a status or a job title, and it must stay one short word because it shares a narrow line with the agent name.
entries.pages.developer.featurePreviewsTab.folde: Label of the Feature Previews switch for the folder-conductor layout in the Sessions sidebar. Default off.

Description under that switch. It must say what turning it on CHANGES (the chat that started a folder's other chats is lifted to the top of that folder, with a coloured bar and a small tag), that this re-orders the Sessions list so the list is unchanged while the switch is off, and that the folder menu's chat item is there either way. The bare word conductor is the literal word the tag shows, so leave it in English and put no quotes or backticks around it -- this description renders as plain text, so any such mark would show on screen.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.range_hours: Segment label on the Telemetry panel's window control meaning a rolling window of the last N HOURS ending now. Keep it as short as a unit abbreviation; it sits in a row of six segments.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.range_days: Segment label on the Telemetry panel's window control meaning a rolling window of the last N DAYS ending now. Keep it as short as a unit abbreviation; it sits in a row of six segments.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.range_default: First segment of the Telemetry panel's time-window control, selected until the reader picks a window: each card then keeps its own built-in reporting period (spend a week, the other cards two weeks). Short, like the other segments.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.range_label: Caption in front of the Telemetry panel's time-window control: the span of time every card on the panel reports over. A noun, not a verb, and not a GUI window.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.range_from: Accessible name of the start-date picker of a custom reporting range. The picked day is included.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.range_to: Accessible name of the end-date picker of a custom reporting range. The picked day is included, so use the inclusive word for an end date.
entries.pages.telemetryPanel.window_range: A custom reporting range shown in each Telemetry card title, e.g. Sep 1, 2026 – Sep 3, 2026. Both dates are already formatted for the locale; keep the separator a dash or the locale's range punctuation.
entries.components.trustDropdown.trust_this_comm: Menu item on the chat approval prompt granting standing permission for ONE exact command that ends sixty minutes after the click. {{cmd}} is shown verbatim and must stay inside the <mono> tag. {{time}} is the local clock time the grant ends, formatted for the user's locale.

Menu item on the chat approval prompt granting standing permission for ONE exact command until midnight in the user's own time zone. {{cmd}} is shown verbatim and must stay inside the <mono> tag. {{time}} is the local clock time the grant ends, formatted for the user's locale.
entries.components.trustDropdown.trust_all_base_: Menu item on the chat approval prompt granting standing permission for the named program(s) run with any arguments, ending sixty minutes after the click. {{base}} is one or more command names joined by ', ' and must stay inside the <mono> tag; "any" means the program run with any arguments. {{time}} is the local clock time the grant ends, formatted for the user's locale.

Menu item on the chat approval prompt granting standing permission for the named program(s) run with any arguments, until midnight in the user's own time zone. {{base}} is one or more command names joined by ', ' and must stay inside the <mono> tag; "any" means the program run with any arguments. {{time}} is the local clock time the grant ends, formatted for the user's locale.
entries.components.trustDropdown.trust_this_comm: Menu item on the chat approval prompt granting standing permission for ONE exact command until the chat session ends, shown beside the hour and rest-of-today rows so its lifetime is stated too. {{cmd}} must stay inside the <mono> tag.
entries.components.trustDropdown.trust_all_base_: Menu item on the chat approval prompt granting standing permission for the named program(s) run with any arguments, until the chat session ends. {{base}} is one or more command names joined by ', ' and must stay inside the <mono> tag; "any" means the program run with any arguments.
entries.components.chatInput.trusted_command_unt: Status line above the chat composer after the user trusts ONE exact command for a limited time: {{cmd}} is that command, possibly shortened, and {{time}} the local clock time the grant ends, after which the command asks for approval again.
entries.components.chatInput.trusted_base_until: Status line above the chat composer after the user trusts the named program(s), run with any arguments, for a limited time: {{base}} is one or more command names, quoted so they read as code, and {{time}} the local clock time the grant ends, after which they ask for approval again.
entries.pages.membersPage.dashboard_owner_only: Shown in a mate's Dashboard tab to a dashboard user who is not that mate's owner. The page holds the mate's task titles, so only the owner may read it. Calm, not an error: there is nothing to retry.
entries.pages.chat.compactionCard.after_turn: Calm status line shown in the chat while the agent is still working, once the conversation's context use has passed the auto-compact threshold (the same setting as 'Auto-Compact Threshold'). {{pct}} is the context use and {{limit}} the threshold, both as percents. Nothing is lost: when the agent's current turn ends, earlier messages are condensed into a summary to free space. The reader does not need to act.
entries.pages.settings.appModels.title: Heading of the Settings > Chat > Model group that lists one model picker per installed app; 'Apps' means the user's installed apps.
entries.pages.settings.appModels.failed_to_save: Inline error after a per-app model pick failed to save; {{app}} is the app's display name.
entries.pages.settings.appModels.inherit_named: Option in each app's model picker meaning 'pick nothing here and use the Default Model setting'; {{model}} is that model's id and is never translated. Not a verb telling the user to act.
entries.pages.settings.appModels.inherit_auto: Same option as inherit_named when the Default Model setting is unset, so the provider picks; 'auto' names that automatic choice.
entries.pages.chatPage.no_session_named: Error notice above the chat composer after the user opened a dashboard link that names a chat session by its short name (for example /chat?sid=chat-7) and no session, open or earlier, has that name. {{name}} is that short name, shown verbatim (for example chat-7). The second sentence suggests two ways forward: check the link, or start a new chat. 'Session' is a chat/agent conversation, never a login session.
entries.pages.chatPage.short_name_also_names: First line of a notice above the chat composer after such a short-name link (for example chat-7) matched several sessions: the oldest was opened, and a list of the other sessions with the same name follows this line, each a clickable session title with its full key and its 'started' date. {{title}} is the title of the session that opened, in quotation marks; {{date}} is the date that chat session was created (started), already formatted -- not its last activity, which is what the sidebar shows, so keep the word for 'started' explicit. {{name}} is the short name, verbatim. The line is a complete sentence and must not end with a colon; the list sits below it, as separate elements. 'Session' is a chat/agent conversation, never a login session.
entries.pages.chatPage.short_name_started: Date label on each row of the list below pages.chatPage.short_name_also_names, after the session title and its key. {{date}} is the date that chat session was created (started), already formatted. It is contrasted with the sidebar, which shows each session's last-activity time, so translate 'started' as 'began / was created', not 'last active' or 'updated'. Use the same wording as the '(started {{date}})' in short_name_also_names.
entries.apps.codeReviewSage.components.reportVie: Code Review Sage report row, muted line next to the severity pills, shown only under a band filter after a dismissal changed the row's band: the row now belongs to the named band ({{band}} is the translated band label, e.g. "Worth a glance") but its POSITION in the list is kept until the user changes the band filter.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.broadcast_preset_all: Broadcast message panel: a quick pick that sends the message to every open session; a short label followed by a live count.
entries.pages.chatSidebar.broadcast_tag: Broadcast message panel: label of the dropdown that narrows recipients to sessions carrying one sidebar tag (a session label, not a version tag).
entries.components.welcomeView.suggestion_daily_: Starter card on the empty chat's welcome screen; clicking it puts this text in the message box as the user's own request to the assistant, asking it to set up a reminder that repeats every day (a note the assistant sends on a schedule, not a calendar event).
entries.components.welcomeView.suggestion_review: Starter card on the welcome screen whose text becomes the user's message asking the assistant to look over the edits the user most recently made to their own code or files; 'changes' means those edits, not product updates or release notes.
entries.components.welcomeView.suggestion_what_n: Starter card on the welcome screen whose text becomes the user's own question to the assistant about which task the user should pick up next; keep it a question in the user's voice, ending with the language's question mark.
entries.components.agentDropdownList.own_memory: Second line of a chat agent picker row for a mate that shares its name with a custom agent: picking this row runs on the mate's own memory store, not the shared one. A short noun phrase, not a sentence.
entries.components.agentDropdownList.shared_memo: Second line of a chat agent picker row when a mate and a custom agent share a name: picking this row runs on the shared default memory store. A short noun phrase, not a sentence.
entries.components.agentDropdownList.label_own_m: Composer agent chip and session-list label for a session on a mate that shares its name with a custom agent; {{label}} is the agent's name, and the suffix says the session runs on the mate's own memory.
entries.components.agentDropdownList.label_share: Composer agent chip and session-list label for a session whose agent name is shared by a mate and a custom agent; {{label}} is the agent's name, and the suffix says the session runs on the shared default memory.
entries.apps.papyrus.page.paper_name: Field label for the name a paper is LISTED under. Not a filename and not the paper's directory: renaming here changes only the displayed name.
entries.apps.papyrus.page.rename_paper: Verb on the button that edits the name a paper is listed under. {{name}} is the paper's current displayed name.
entries.apps.papyrus.page.rename_title_rejected: Error banner in the Papyrus paper list after a rename was refused because the typed name had no visible characters left once invisible ones were removed. {{name}} is the paper's folder name (for example 6a16ddbf), which the list shows again when the field is cleared. 'Clear the field' means delete everything typed in it.
entries.apps.papyrus.page.rename_config_refused: Error banner in the Papyrus paper list after a rename could not be saved because the paper's own settings could not be written. 'Settings' means this paper's stored options, not app-wide settings.
entries.apps.papyrus.page.rename_paper_replaced: Error banner in the Papyrus paper list after a rename was refused because the paper was deleted and recreated under the same folder name since the list loaded. The list has already reloaded; 'Enter' is the keyboard key.
entries.components.jobForm.runs_as: Label above a two-option switch in the scheduled-job form that chooses what the job runs as: a custom agent or a mate.
entries.components.jobForm.runs_as_custom_agent: Switch option in the scheduled-job form: the job opens a new session on a custom agent (an agent template). Keep it short; it sits in a segmented control.
entries.components.jobForm.runs_as_crewmate: Switch option in the scheduled-job form: the job is delivered to one mate (a named member of the crew). Use the same word as the Mates page.
entries.components.jobForm.runs_as_custom_agent_: Line under the switch when Custom agent is chosen: the job runs in a chat of its own, which it reuses on every run, with shared (global) memory.
entries.components.jobForm.runs_as_crewmate_hint: Line under the switch when Mate is chosen. {{name}} is the mate's name. The job runs in that mate's chat with the mate's own memory and files (its workspace), and also shows on its Mates page.
entries.components.jobForm.runs_as_fixed: Line under the switch when editing a job, explaining why the other option is greyed out: a job cannot switch between custom agent and mate after it is created.
entries.components.jobForm.runs_as_no_crewmates: Line under the switch, explaining why the Mate option is greyed out: the user has no mates yet, and says where to add one (the Mates page).
entries.components.jobForm.time_limit: Label of a number field in the scheduled-job (cron) form. How long one run of the job may take before it is stopped. A noun phrase, not an action.
entries.components.jobForm.time_limit_descriptio: Help text under that field, also its tooltip. Explains that a run still going after this many minutes is stopped and reported as timed out, that the limit covers the whole run, and the 30-minute default.
entries.components.jobForm.time_limit_minutes: Accessible name of that number field; the value is a whole number of minutes.
entries.components.gitPanel.repos_empty: Empty state of the Git side-panel tab when the gateway has found no Git repository for this chat. Two sentences: nothing to show, then how a repository joins the list (the agent edits files or runs commands in it). Prospective wording only: say how a row appears, never what the chat did or did not do in the past, and not "yet". "Git" is the tool name - do not translate.
entries.components.gitPanel.repos_loading: Status text beside a spinner in the Git side-panel tab while the list of this chat's repositories is being fetched for the first time. Sentence case, ends in an ellipsis.
entries.components.gitPanel.source_project: Small tag after a repository's folder path in the Git tab, marking the chat's own project folder. One short noun.
entries.components.gitPanel.source_project_help: Tooltip on the "Project" tag in the Git tab. Two sentences: the first says what the tag means (the tagged repository is the one this chat was started in, its project repository); the second says what the untagged rows are (repositories the agent worked in during this chat), because the tag alone does not explain them.
entries.components.gitPanel.repos_caption_projec: Second sentence appended after components.gitPanel.repos_caption, shown only when the chat's own project repository is one of the listed repositories: it tells the reader the project's repository sits at the top of the list. A short standalone sentence that reads on from the caption.
entries.components.gitPanel.section_expand_hint: Short muted hint right after the repository path in a COLLAPSED repository heading in the Git tab, telling the reader that clicking the heading opens the section's uncommitted changes and commit history. Shown only while the section is closed; wraps under the path in a narrow panel. Also used as the native title tooltip on every collapsed heading. A short action phrase, no trailing punctuation.
entries.components.gitPanel.section_collapse_hin: Native title tooltip on an OPEN repository heading in the Git tab; clicking the heading folds away that section's uncommitted changes and commit history. A short action phrase, no trailing punctuation. Mirror of components.gitPanel.section_expand_hint (the collapsed-heading tooltip).
entries.components.gitPanel.repos_caption: One-line muted caption above the Git tab's repository list, always shown. States the SAME rule as the empty state: the rows are repositories the agent edited files in or ran commands in during this chat (reading a file does not add one). Visible without hovering. "Git" is the tool name - do not translate.
entries.components.gitPanel.repos_incomplete: Muted informational status beneath the Git tab repository list, not an error or action. Says the list may be incomplete: some repositories the agent worked in are not shown because bounded tracking dropped them from an executed action, and each returns to the list once the agent works in it again in a recorded way. Do not imply a known missing-repository count: omitted counts discovered roots separately. Render once per snapshot, even when no repository is listed.
entries.components.gitPanel.repos_omitted_one: Informational status (not an error) beneath the Git tab's repository list, in two clauses. First, what the list counts: the agent worked in {{formattedTotal}} distinct repositories in all (a localized number: the rows shown plus the ones omitted), and the {{formattedLimit}} most recent of them are the ones listed (the server's cap, localized). Second, how a hidden repository reappears: it re-enters the list on its own the next time the agent edits a file or runs a command in it. It is a fixed rule, not an action - there is no way to reveal the rest, so the copy must not read as a link or offer one, and avoid the word "older" (it collides with the sidebar's Older Sessions). count (the number omitted) selects the plural form. Singular form: one hidden repository.
entries.components.gitPanel.repos_omitted_other: Plural of repos_omitted_one: the agent worked in {{formattedTotal}} repositories in all, the {{formattedLimit}} most recent are listed, and each hidden one reappears by itself once the agent works in it again. Informational, not an error, not an action; avoid "older". Both numbers are already localized; count (the number omitted) selects the plural form.
entries.components.gitPanel.repos_retry: Button inside the Git tab's listing-failed notice that fetches the repository list again. One word, imperative.
entries.components.gitPanel.repos_failed: Error shown in the Git tab when the list of repositories this chat works in could not be loaded.
entries.components.gitPanel.repos_refresh_failed: Notice above a repository list that is still shown after its background refresh failed; says the refresh failed and that the shown list may be stale. Not an action.
entries.app.release_notes_not_published_yet: Notice in the post-update "What's new" dialog. {{release}} is the release the user is running (e.g. 0.8.0) whose notes are not written yet; {{shown}} is the older release (e.g. 0.7.1) whose notes are displayed instead. Both are bare version numbers.
entries.app.focus_mode_on_announce: Spoken by a screen reader when focus mode turns on and the chrome becomes unreachable. {{chord}} is the user's live key chord in ARIA spelling (e.g. Alt+Shift+M); keep it verbatim.
entries.pages.schedulePage.type_crewmate: Line 1 of the Type cell in the Schedule list for a job that is a mate's own schedule (runs in that mate's chat). Singular noun, same word as the Mates page.
entries.pages.schedulePage.filter_by_crewmate: Accessible name of the dropdown next to the Schedule list's search box that narrows the list to one mate's schedules.
entries.pages.schedulePage.all_crewmates: First row of that dropdown, which shows every job (no mate filter).
entries.lib.speechProviders.unavailable_no_reaso: Status line under the Settings speech provider picker when the selected add-on provider cannot run and sent no reason of its own.
entries.lib.speechProviders.sign_in_hint: Hint under the Settings speech provider picker; {{account}} is the provider's own account name, such as 'Acme account', and is never translated.
entries.pages.settings.sttSettings.status_unavai: Status badge on Settings > Voice speech-to-text when the selected add-on provider cannot run right now (for example, not signed in); it is installed, so not 'not installed'.
entries.components.startupVideoModal.crewmates_t: Headline of the 'Meet your Mates.' launch dialog, in large poster type. 'Mates' is the product's name for a person's crewmates (AI teammates); keep the word as the Mates page names them, plural. Ends with a full stop, as a tagline.
entries.components.startupVideoModal.crewmates_d: The one line under crewmates_title. 'They' are the Mates: they find work to do on their own, do it, and only come to the user when they need a decision. Keep it to one sentence.
entries.components.startupVideoModal.new_tag: Small badge pill on a sidebar navigation item, marking a feature the user has not opened yet. An ADJECTIVE meaning 'recently added', not the verb 'create'. Very tight space: keep it to one short word.
entries.components.startupVideoModal.not_now: Secondary button of the launch dialog: close it for now; the page it introduces gets a 'New' tag instead. Short.
entries.components.startupVideoModal.try_now: Primary button of the launch dialog: open the Mates page right away. Imperative, two short words if the language allows.
entries.components.meetYourMatesIntro.sample_lin: First bubble of a SAMPLE chat message from a Mate inside the launch dialog, showing what a Mate says after working unattended overnight: it found an unreliable ('flaky') test and fixed it. First person, past tense, casual.
Second bubble of the same sample message: the pull request is ready, and the Mate asks whether to merge it. 'PR' stays as the abbreviation developers use.
entries.components.meetYourMatesIntro.sample_mer: Primary pill under the sample message, the answer that tells the Mate to merge the pull request. Imperative, one or two words. Decorative in the dialog, not a real button.
entries.components.meetYourMatesIntro.sample_sho: Secondary pill under the sample message, the answer that asks to see the change before merging. Imperative, short. Decorative in the dialog, not a real button.
entries.pages.membersPage.entrance_first_mate: Speech bubble under Mate's large face the first time its chat opens, before it flies into the header and greets; said only while Mate is the only mate on the roster. Mate is the product's name for the standing teammate agent; keep the teammate word the catalog already uses for it.
entries.pages.membersPage.entrance_hello: The same speech bubble when the roster already holds other mates; {{name}} is Mate's display name and is never translated.
entries.pages.settings.instancesPanel.restart_to: Warning banner in Settings -> Remote Crew (and the older Instances panel) shown when remote crew management is turned on but the gateway has not been restarted yet. <restartCmd/> renders the literal CLI command as monospace code -- keep the tag and do not translate it. 'a terminal' is a command-line shell window; 'the computer this dashboard runs on' is the machine whose gateway serves this page, as opposed to the remote crews listed below it, and it may not be the device showing this page.
entries.pages.membersPage.on_its_own: Section header on a crewmate's Schedules tab, over what wakes the crewmate WITHOUT a schedule the user set (its patrol over tasks it handed out). 'Its' refers to the crewmate; keep it short, title-like.
entries.pages.membersPage.your_schedules: Section header over the list of schedules the user set for this crewmate, shown under the 'On its own' header. 'Your' is the user.
entries.pages.membersPage.patrol_name: Row title: the crewmate is keeping watch over the tasks it handed out to helpers. 'Its' refers to the crewmate.
entries.pages.membersPage.patrol_wakes: Second line of that row: the crewmate wakes when one of its tasks reports back, and otherwise at most every {{interval}} (a short duration like '15m').
entries.pages.membersPage.patrol_pause: Verb on a button: pause the crewmate's watch over its tasks. Not the noun.
entries.pages.membersPage.patrol_resume: Verb on a button: resume a paused watch. Not the noun.
entries.pages.membersPage.patrol_stopped_runtime: One-phrase reason the watch stopped: it ran up to its time budget of {{limit}} (a short duration like '7d').
entries.pages.membersPage.patrol_stopped_cycles: One-phrase reason the watch stopped: it did as many checks as it was allowed.
entries.components.markdownPanel.select_any_text: One-time tip at the top of the file viewer, shown only when the device has a mouse or trackpad: the reader can select text, or drag a box across an image, to add comments, then send them to the chat together. On a touch-only device the text-only tip shows instead.
entries.components.commentOverlay.comment_on_the: Accessible name of the text field in the comment box for a box drawn on an image in the file viewer (also opened by the keyboard 'Comment on this image' button). It parallels the text composer's 'Comment on the selected text', so the field and its 'Add comment' button never read the same; 'boxed area' is the part of the image inside the drawn box.
entries.components.commentOverlay.image_anchor: Label on a pending comment in the file viewer that is attached to a box drawn on an image rather than to text; {{number}} is the box's number, the same one drawn on the box over the image and the comment's place in the pending list, already formatted, and {{label}} is the image alt text, or its file name when it has none.
entries.components.imageComments.comment_on_imag: Accessible name and tooltip of a button on a rendered image in the file viewer that appears only when it has keyboard focus; pressing it opens a comment on the whole image, for readers who cannot drag a box across it.
entries.components.imageComments.box_label: Accessible name of a box drawn on an image for an existing comment; {{number}} is the comment number in the pending list, and {{x}}, {{y}} are the box's top-left corner as horizontal and vertical percentages, already formatted. Activating it highlights that comment in the pending list.
entries.components.markdownPanel.new_badge: Small badge before 'Tip:' on the file viewer's one-time comment tip, shown only when the tip is back for a reader who had closed its earlier, text-only wording: it marks that the tip now names a new feature (drawing a box on an image to comment on it). An adjective for the feature, not a verb like 'Create'; keep it to one short word.
entries.pages.mcpManagement.details_env: Settings > MCP, a server row's Details: label before the list of environment variable NAMES the server's launch sets (never their values). Short for 'environment'.
entries.pages.mcpManagement.details_new: Settings > MCP, a paused server's Details and the Review dialog: heading over the server's NEW launch command, shown beside the 'Before' (previously approved) one. An adjective for the launch, not a 'create' action.
entries.crewWorkerKit.apply: Button in a crewmate's Add abilities pane that writes the previewed abilities into the crewmate. Imperative verb "add", not a heading.
entries.crewWorkerKit.change_added: Small badge on one row of the Add abilities preview: this item is new to the mate and will be added. A passive status label (an adjective, like "Already has" beside it), not an action or a button; keep it to one short word.
entries.crewWorkerKit.change_skipped: Small badge on one row of the Add abilities preview: the crewmate already has this item, so it is left out.
entries.crewEditorNext.band_comes_with: Heading of the read-only list of abilities a crewmate gets from Kiro Crew itself; {{name}} is the crewmate's name.
entries.crewEditorNext.band_added: Heading of the list of abilities added to this crewmate on top of what it comes with; {{name}} is the crewmate's name.
entries.crewEditorNext.band_remove: Button on one row of the Added list that removes that ability from the crewmate. Imperative verb.
entries.crewEditorNext.band_remove_confirm_title: Title of the confirmation shown after pressing Remove on one row of the Added list; {{name}} is the ability's name as the row shows it. A yes/no question, not a heading.
entries.crewWorkerKit.retry: Button shown after the Add abilities preview failed; runs the preview again for the same agent.
entries.crewWorkerKit.done_added: Confirmation shown in a crewmate's Add abilities pane after an add succeeds. {{count}} is how many items were added; {{name}} is the crewmate's display name.
entries.crewWorkerKit.done_approvals: Second sentence of that confirmation, shown only when the add granted tool approvals. "Auto-approvals" is the name of the group in the preview the user just saw.
entries.crewWorkerKit.open_approvals: Button next to that confirmation that opens the crewmate editor's Approvals section. "Approvals" is that section's tab name.
entries.crewWorkerKit.group_directions: Heading of the Add abilities preview group for an agent's behavior directions: the instructions the crewmate's worker follows after its own built-in prompt. A crewmate holds one set; adding another agent's replaces it.
entries.crewWorkerKit.change_replaced: Small badge on the behavior-directions row of the Add abilities preview: these directions will replace the ones the crewmate has now. Same register as the "New" badge.
entries.crewEditorNext.band_directions: Heading of the group in a crewmate's Abilities section that shows its behavior directions (instructions its worker follows after its built-in prompt). Same term as the Add abilities preview group.
entries.crewWorkerKit.dont_add: Button at the bottom of the Add abilities preview, beside the add button: closes the preview without adding anything. It sits above the editor's own Cancel and Save, so it names what it declines (adding the previewed abilities) rather than reading "Cancel".
entries.crewWorkerKit.preview_replaces: Heading of the Add abilities preview when the picked agent's behavior directions will replace the ones the crewmate has now and nothing else is new. {{template}} is the agent's name. A crewmate holds one set of directions, so this is an overwrite, not an addition.
entries.crewWorkerKit.preview_replaces_adds: Heading of the Add abilities preview when the picked agent's behavior directions will replace the crewmate's current ones AND other items are new. {{count}} is how many new items are added (the replaced directions are not counted); {{template}} is the agent's name.
entries.crewWorkerKit.apply_replace: Button at the bottom of the Add abilities preview when the only change is replacing the crewmate's behavior directions. Imperative verb "replace".
entries.crewWorkerKit.apply_replace_n: Button at the bottom of the Add abilities preview when it replaces the crewmate's behavior directions and adds new items. {{count}} is how many new items are added (the replaced directions are not counted). Imperative.
entries.crewWorkerKit.current_directions: Muted line on the behavior-directions row of the Add abilities preview, under the incoming directions. {{directions}} is the crewmate's current directions text, which the incoming directions will overwrite.
entries.crewWorkerKit.done_replaced: Sentence in the confirmation after an add succeeds, shown when it replaced the crewmate's behavior directions. May follow the "Added N to NAME." sentence or stand alone.
entries.crewEditorNext.band_remove_stale: Error in the mate abilities view when Remove is refused because the displayed revision changed; nothing was removed, the list refreshes, and the user must check it and press the Remove button again.
entries.pages.developer.agentBackendTab.pi: Name of the Pi coding-agent harness, shown wherever an agent harness is named (Settings > Agent Harness, a mate's Harness setting). A product name: keep it in Latin script, unchanged; not the mathematical constant.
